title: What ‘Optimizing Search and Siri’ Means in iOS 27 and How to Speed It Up
snippet: Your iPhone will still work, but the process may take some time.
fullText:
If you’ve updated your iPhone to iOS 27, don’t be alarmed if you see a message that reads “Optimizing Search and Siri” in Settings. The message means iOS is rebuilding its search index, a necessary process after this major iOS update because the update implements a brand-new search infrastructure, and the system cannot simply update your existing index. It must crawl through your entire storage drive from scratch.

You can download iOS 27 now by going to Settings > General > Software Update > Update Now and following the prompts on your screen.

At June’s Worldwide Developers Conference, Apple announced that it was rebuilding its Search interface for iOS 27. The company said the restructure would make searching across your device faster, more reliable and more accurate. In order to do that, iOS 27 has to reindex items across your iPhone. So after you update, you’ll see a banner in Settings that reads “Optimizing Search and Siri.” This is a normal part of the update, and it could take a while to finish, but the good news is you can still use your iPhone during this process.

Here’s what you need to know about the indexing and optimization process once you download iOS 27.

What is indexing?

Data indexing is the process of scanning and organizing metadata from data assets into an index so it can be easily searched.

“Think of it like the index of a book,” data management company Komprise wrote online. “[The index] doesn’t hold the content, but it tells you where to find it, and what’s inside.”

Apple’s support page about Spotlight indexing says that Spotlight search indexes your iPhone when you first set up your device, as data changes on your device and after you update your iPhone. So your device has reindexed before and you likely never noticed – I know I didn’t.

Apple also notes that your iPhone’s index “stays on your device and isn’t shared with Apple or your other devices.” 

Indexing can take hours or days

You can still use your iPhone, even when it’s indexing.LuckyDuck via Getty Images

Apple’s support page notes that indexing could take anywhere from a couple hours to a few days. When I updated my iPhone to a beta version of iOS 27, my iPhone took a couple hours to index, but the more stuff you have stored on your phone, the longer it will take. 

The process takes longer this time around because Apple rebuilt its Search interface in iOS 27. So the update isn’t just adding a few more things to the index, it’s implementing a new search system. 

That means the system isn’t just crawling through the new stuff — it needs to go back through all the data in your phone. Think of it like cataloging new items you’ve bought versus creating an inventory of everything in your home.

Apple does offer a few suggestions on how to speed up the process:

Plug your device into a power source.

Connect your device to Wi-Fi.

Don’t use your iPhone.

OK, can I still use my iPhone?

You can! Indexing doesn’t prevent you from using your iPhone, but it goes faster if you set the phone aside.

If you do use your iPhone during the process, your Spotlight search results might be incomplete because it hasn’t finished indexing. Otherwise, your device should operate as usual. Which is good because I couldn’t imagine going without my phone for a few days at this point – don’t judge me. 

Spotlight search still not working? 

If your iPhone is finished indexing – the banner in Settings will go away – and you’re still running into issues, you should review your Search settings and make sure Spotlight has access to your apps. Here’s how to check. 

Tap Settings.

Tap Search.

From here, you can adjust what shows up in Spotlight, and near the bottom of the menu, you can review which apps Spotlight has access to. You can tap into each app to grant or revoke Spotlight permission. 

However, there doesn’t seem to be a way to grant or revoke Spotlight access across all apps at once, so you have to go into each individual app to do this. 

For more on Apple, here’s what to know about iOS 27, the iPhone Duo and everything Apple announced at its “Surprise and shine” event.

title: Google goes in-depth, and a bit NSFW, on Noto 3D emoji as Android rollout expands
snippet: Google Design published a more detailed explanation of Noto 3D today as it expands beyond Pixel devices. more…
fullText:
Google Design published a more detailed explanation of Noto 3D today as it expands beyond Pixel devices.

Google explains that the design process for Noto 3D involved “drawing, sculpting, and debating every single character by hand so that dimension never came at the cost of soul.”

Noto 3D prioritizes “emotional clarity” over “treating emoji as miniature scans of the natural world.”

Our job was to preserve the vibe behind each symbol: using 3D to give the character a body, but illustration to give it a soul.

Research found that “highly anatomical details like irises or nostril depth actually slow down how fast our brains process emotion,” so the aim was to remove “extraneous detail and [keep] facial geometry minimal.” Additionally, “excessive props and texture destroy comprehension,” with “background features and accessories” becoming “visual static” at 18×18 pixels.

	

The design team ultimately decided that “every emoji gets at most three essential details to communicate what it is.”

In going from flat assets to three dimensions, Google asked: “What does the back of a smiley face look like?” NSFW (truly) joke aside, the team found examples like how the poodle emoji only had three legs.

Meanwhile, the same research found that “people empathize far more with complete silhouettes — especially when it comes to depicting real animals.” As such, Google moved away from floating heads. 

Seeing an animal’s stance, paws, and posture helps communicate intent. Upon learning this last year, we updated a few animal emoji, like the raccoon, to embrace its full mischievous self — and now in 3D.

Following the Pixel 11 launch, Noto 3D is now “rolling out across Google apps, Android, and select devices from partners including Nothing, Lenovo, Xiaomi, OPPO, OnePlus, realme, vivo, iQOO, HONOR, TECNO, Infinix, itel, [and] Motorola.” You can also browse the entire collection on Google’s dedicated page.

title: Galaxy S26 series reportedly getting a price hike imminently, could be as much as $100
snippet: In the era of RAMageddon, the price hikes just keep coming. Samsung has left its Galaxy S26 untouched thus far, but a new report suggest prices hikes of around $100 could be on the way. more…
fullText:
In the era of RAMageddon, the price hikes just keep coming. Samsung has left its Galaxy S26 untouched thus far, but a new report suggest prices hikes of around $100 could be on the way.

The Galaxy S26 series launched in February with the base S26 and S26+ seeing slight price bumps from their predecessors, and the Ultra unchanged – $899, $1,099, and $1,299, respectively. But a lot has changed in the time since, and it seems Samsung may be bumping those prices further up.

Hans Economy reports that, at least in Korea, Galaxy S26 prices “will be abruptly raised starting October 1.” The planned price hikes (and their converted pricing in USD) follow:

Galaxy S26: 1,254,000 won > 1,403,600 won ($930~ > $1,040)

Galaxy S26+: 1,452,000 won > 1,601,600 won ($1,077~ > $1,188~)

Galaxy S26 Ultra: 1,797,400 won > 1,947,000 won ($1,334~ > $1,444~)

Apparently, Samsung is making this move based on two factors; the continual rise of component costs, and the fact that Apple also just hiked its iPhone prices. The latest iPhone 18 Pro launches are more expensive while the iPhone 17 also saw a $100 price hike in the US (more on 9to5Mac), with the lineup now starting at $899 in the US and 1,450,000 won in South Korea.

	

With that comparison in mind, it’s harder to imagine Samsung plans to bring these price hikes to the US, as they’d make Galaxy flagships $100 more expensive than iPhones across the board, but anything’s possible. 

Samsung, commenting on the report, says that “nothing has been finalized” yet (translated):

We have not sent out any official notice regarding a price increase for the Galaxy S26 series… While it is true that we are internally reviewing whether to adjust prices in consideration of cost burdens, such as the recent rise in component prices, nothing has been finalized as of now.

title: Google Maps rolling out Android Auto speed limits and speedometer that show even without navigation
snippet: While the speedometer has been hit or miss for some Android Auto users as of late, Google Maps is now confirmed to be rolling out speed limits and a speedometer that show at all times, even when you don’t have a destination selected. more…
fullText:
While the speedometer has been hit or miss for some Android Auto users as of late, Google Maps is now confirmed to be rolling out speed limits and a speedometer that show at all times, even when you don’t have a destination selected.

Speed limits in Google Maps launched back in 2019, with the live speedometer appearing later and only starting to show up on Android Auto a few months ago. Earlier this month, though, the speedometer vanished for some users. 

Google is now confirming two things.

First, the disappearing speedometer is being investigated by the Android Auto team. In other words, it appears to be a bug of some kind rather than an intentional removal or rollback of the feature.

	
	

More interesting, though, is that Google is rolling out the ability to see the speed limit of the current road as well as the live speedometer on Maps via Android Auto even when a destination is not set. There have been intermittent reports of this for a few weeks now, but Google is confirming that it’s actually rolling out.

…the ability to have the speedometer, speed limit, and traffic signals/stop signs showing without a destination set is still rolling out. Thus, not everyone will have this particular feature yet.

The exact timeline for when this will be widely available remains to be seen, but it’s great to see nonetheless. Drivers are very often using Google Maps navigation, but shorter or more familiar trips don’t always require setting a destination – but it’s still nice to see speed limits and the speedometer at those times.

title: Android Auto update lets you customize your Google Maps ‘driving avatar’ via car display
snippet: Google is rolling out an update for Maps on Android Auto that gives users the ability to edit their “driving avatar” directly from the car’s display. more…
fullText:
Google is rolling out an update for Maps on Android Auto that gives users the ability to edit their “driving avatar” directly from the car’s display.

The ability to change the classic blue arrow navigation icon in Google Maps itself is not new, but it’s only been available on car displays for about a year. In May 2025, Google Maps rolled out support for showing your chosen icon on Android Auto and CarPlay, but it needed to be set on the phone itself. 

Now, Google is rolling out an on-car picker for your Google Maps “driving avatar” on Android Auto.

The change is rather simple. Through Google Maps on Android Auto, a new “driving avatar” setting appears alongside settings for home/work and alerts. Tapping it gives you the option to pick your avatar and change it to the color of your choice. It’s the same functionality found on your phone, just now accessible directly via the car’s display.

	

This appears to be going live with a server-side update. Android Authority spotted the change with Android Auto 17.8.163744 and Google Maps 26.38.01.980791571 but, despite using those same versions, we’re not seeing the option just yet. Sound off in the comments below if you have it.

In our teardown of Android Auto 17.8, we also noticed that Google has removed the neat little “Jimothy” Easter egg which, as we predicted, was clearly never meant for a public-facing rollout.

title: Apple explains how the iPhone 18 Pro’s new Reference Image camera mode works
snippet: A new post on Apple’s Security Research blog details the fascinating tech, architecture, and thinking behind the iPhone 18 Pro’s new Reference Image camera mode. Here are the details more…
fullText:
A new post on Apple’s Security Research blog details the fascinating tech, architecture, and thinking behind the iPhone 18 Pro’s new Reference Image camera mode. Here are the details

Apple explains why it developed the new Reference Image camera mode

In a blog post titled “Apple Reference Image: A New Approach for Verified Photography,” Apple goes in-depth into how its new photographic authenticity system works.

The post confirms that the company’s motivation to build Apple Reference Image was the ever-lowering barrier to creating or adjusting images synthetically.

Apple explains that while industry standards such as C2PA help address the problem, they remain vulnerable to compromise at points in the editing chain.

For this reason, Apple developed a fascinatingly creative chain-of-verification system that is private, secure, and, to the company’s knowledge, “the only image provenance system that provides quantum-secure defenses.”

‘A new standard for verifiable digital photography’

In its explanation, Apple uses classic photography terms, such as a secure digital negative, which contains the raw captured pixels along with information such as signed metadata and timestamps, and is developed in a secure, private, and verifiable environment within the company’s Private Cloud Compute structure.

This semantic authenticity is just one of the three core requirements Apple says a high-assurance photographic provenance system must meet, the other two being resilience to compromise and privacy preservation.

If Apple’s confidence scoring system identifies a sensor as low-scoring and that sensor is revoked, Private Cloud Compute will no longer sign Reference Images captured by it.

Likewise, individual Reference Images can be revoked if later determined to be fraudulent, with Apple devices regularly fetching updated revocation lists.

Another interesting aspect of the Apple Reference Image chain of trust is that it begins once a camera sensor is first initialized, during the iPhone’s manufacturing process.

The sensor generates a signing key pair, keeping the private key to itself while sharing the public verification key with the factory recording station, which then signs it with a factory certificate authority and records it in the device’s hardware manifest.

That private key will later be used to sign every photo taken in Reference Image mode, binding the captured pixel data and sensor metadata to that specific camera sensor before the image ever reaches iOS for further processing.

Apple also uses cryptographic timestamps to establish a verifiable window for when each photo was taken. Instead of relying on a timestamp provided by the device’s general operating system, which the company says can be compromised, the iPhone periodically receives a secure timestamp token that serves as a lower bound.

It then requests another after capture to establish an upper bound, allowing Apple to verify that the image was captured sometime between the two.

The Secure Enclave also plays a role by signing metadata that originates outside the camera sensor. Private Cloud Compute later verifies those signatures, confirms that the sensor and Secure Enclave belong to the same iPhone, and checks the timestamps before developing the secure digital negative.

Once those checks pass, Private Cloud Compute processes the negative into the final JPEG Reference Image and signs it using a combination of traditional and post-quantum cryptography, which Apple says is designed to keep the image verifiable even against future quantum attacks.

Apple goes on to explain that the Reference Image framework was designed so that an outside observer cannot determine the identity of the photographer, which device took a given photo, or whether the same device captured two Reference Images.

This is particularly important, Apple notes, for photographers working in sensitive environments, such as conflict zones, where proving an image is authentic should not require giving up anonymity.

This Security Research blog post makes for a truly fascinating read, even if you are not a technical person. You can read it here.

title: Lukewarm orders for iPhone 18 Pro, says analyst – but it doesn’t mean much
snippet: A high-profile analyst has said that demand for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max appears “lukewarm” based on pre-order wait times. Jeff Pu notes that most iPhone 18 Pro configurations are available for immediate delivery and that the longest wait for the most popular iPhone 18 Pro Max extends only to three to four weeks … more…
fullText:
A high-profile analyst has said that demand for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max appears “lukewarm” based on pre-order wait times.

Jeff Pu notes that most iPhone 18 Pro configurations are available for immediate delivery and that the longest wait for the most popular iPhone 18 Pro Max extends only to three to four weeks … 

Pu says that there’s no delay with most iPhone 18 Pro configs, while availability varies for the Pro Max:

Silver 1TB & 2TB models: Immediate

Black/Glacier 1TB: 1-2 weeks

Burgundy 1TB: 3-4 weeks

256GB and 512GB models in most colors: 3-4 weeks

Assuming consistent supply levels, this would indicate that the iPhone 18 Pro is less popular than most of its predecessors. However, there are so many caveats to this that our take is longer than reporting the data …

9to5Mac’s Take

Actual sales data for Apple products is, of course, extremely commercially sensitive, and the company long stopped revealing unit sales even in earnings reports. There are a number of ways analysts and market intelligence companies can try to get a steer on approximate numbers, however.

The most obvious of these is to look at estimated shipping times for new products. This is a very crude metric as what it actually measures is the gap between supply and demand. A million people wanting a new device and a million devices being stockpiled would still equal immediate delivery, while demand for 100,000 units with only 10,000 in stock would mean lengthy wait times.

Market intelligence companies do use other methods to supplement this. A common one is to use pre-recruited consumer panels who have consented to their inboxes being scanned for order emails. Consumer surveys are also sometimes used. A combination of methods can improve reliability, but ultimately it all amounts to educated guesses.

The huge variable this time around, as Pu himself acknowledges, is that we are still waiting for pre-orders to open for the iPhone Duo. An unknown number of those who would otherwise have ordered one of the iPhone 18 Pro models will be waiting for that instead. “Lukewarm” demand for the iPhone 18 Pro could potentially point to higher than expected demand for the iPhone Duo.

Things will get even more complicated once pre-orders do open for the Duo, since reporting has suggested that production yields have been relatively low, meaning that even modest demand could see lengthy waits for shipping.

title: Android Bench 2.0 focuses on long-horizon tasks, agent evaluations
snippet: Google’s development of Android Bench continues today with a version 2.0 that reflects how AI can handle more complex development tasks. more…
fullText:
Google’s development of Android Bench continues today with a version 2.0 that reflects how AI can handle more complex development tasks.

The first version “focused on incremental changes to existing repositories,” like bug fixes or smaller feature requests. Android Bench 2.0 targets “tasks of great complexity that take an engineer multiple days or even a week to complete,” such as adding new features, building apps from scratch, and converting cross-platform apps to Android.

This new focus required “more nuanced evaluation and scoring” that goes beyond pass or fail grading. Google is moving from binary to continuous scoring:

We calculate this completion rate through a combination of factors like functionality, visual fidelity, and avoiding regressions. We also apply objective scoring penalties for deviations from evaluation instructions or structural constraints.

Google has rated Gemini 3.7/3.8 Flash, OpenAI GPT-6, Anthropic Fable 5.1, Kimi K3, and Qwen 3.8 Max. GPT-6 Astra is at the top of the benchmark with a 28% pass rate (compared to scores in the 90% range with the previous approach).

	

Google shared insights like how “porting cross-platform apps to Android remains an open challenge—no model hits a 100% pass rate, and frontier models reach at most a 80% completion rate.”

“…AI does a better job at writing new code rather than refactoring existing code. Refactors and migrations get trickier because success depends on architectural complexity rather than code volume.”

“Models show strong capabilities on well-established, deterministic transformations, such as converting Java to Kotlin, swapping Retrofit for Ktor, or introducing a ViewModel layer.”

“…models struggle when tasks require runtime validation (like missing dependency injection graphs), involve breaking framework changes, or run into knowledge gaps with unreleased libraries.”

With agent evaluations, Android Bench ran “agents from the corresponding model provider,” like Gemini 3.8 Flash on Google Antigravity and GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex. Google says “harness design positively impacts developer outcomes,” with Android Bench planning to include different model and agent combinations in the future.

title: Camp Snap’s 110D gives slim retro film cameras a digital upgrade
snippet: Camp Snap is expanding its small collection of screenless digital point-and-shoot cameras with the new pocket-friendly 110D featuring a thin horizontal design first popularized by Kodak film cameras in the 1970s. The Camp Snap 110D is available for preorder starting today for $74.95 in back in black (black and gray) or dreamsicle (white and orange) color options with matching accessories. The Camp Snap 110D's design is inspired by the myriad of low-cost cameras from companies like Canon, Minolta, and Pentax that used the 110 film cartridges Kodak first introduced in 1972. The cartridges were easy for even novice photographers to use and cou … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Andrew Liszewski

 

is a senior reporter who’s been covering and reviewing the latest gadgets and tech since 2006, but has loved all things electronic since he was a kid.

Camp Snap is expanding its small collection of screenless digital point-and-shoot cameras with the new pocket-friendly 110D featuring a thin horizontal design first popularized by Kodak film cameras in the 1970s. The Camp Snap 110D is available for preorder starting today for $74.95 in back in black (black and gray) or dreamsicle (white and orange) color options with matching accessories.

The Camp Snap 110D’s design is inspired by the myriad of low-cost cameras from companies like Canon, Minolta, and Pentax that used the 110 film cartridges Kodak first introduced in 1972. The cartridges were easy for even novice photographers to use and could be developed using existing machines already capable of processing 16mm motion picture film. Lomography is one of the last companies to still manufacture 110 film, but the Camp Snap 110D offers a similar experience with the convenience of digital.

Like the Camp Snap 2 that launched last June, the 110D isn’t a megapixel powerhouse. It uses an 8-megapixel Sony 1/3.2-inch CMOS sensor paired with a 4.2mm, f/2.0 lens that’s compatible with 30.5mm screw-on filters if you want to experiment with wide-angle or macro photography. If you’re after a matching retro look for your photos, the 110D includes five built-in software filters with vintage, analog, and black and white effects that are selectable using a sliding switch.

The 4GB bundled microSD card, which is stored behind a screw-secured door so kids can’t find it, can store up to 2,000 photos before you need to copy them off to a mobile device or PC over USB-C. The 110D’s 800mAh battery has enough capacity for around 500 shots while an automatic sleep mode that quickly wakes the camera when the shutter button is pressed helps prevent unwanted battery drain without having to constantly power the 110D off an on.

Other features include a built-in flash with adjustable color temperature and a basic segmented LCD display on the back showing remaining battery life and the number of photos you’ve taken.

title: Tim Cook keeping John Ternus away from controversy by attending White House dinner
snippet: One of the trickier parts of Tim Cook’s job when he was Apple CEO was walking the tightrope of upholding the company’s values without provoking the ire of the White House over things like immigration policy and DEI. His new role as executive chairman sees him retain responsibility for government liaison, offering replacement CEO John Ternus some degree of protection … more…
fullText:
One of the trickier parts of Tim Cook’s job when he was Apple CEO was walking the tightrope of upholding the company’s values without provoking the ire of the White House over things like immigration policy and DEI.

His new role as executive chairman sees him retain responsibility for government liaison, offering replacement CEO John Ternus some degree of protection … 

Past challenges

The challenges Cook faced in the past date back many years. For example, back in 2018, changes to US immigration policy and practice affected thousands of Apple employees. Tim Cook was among a number of CEOs who wrote to the administration stating that the changes were causing “considerable anxiety for many thousands of Apple employees,” as well as “threatening to disrupt company operations.”

Cook faced similar difficulties last year when Trump said that Apple should get rid of its DEI policies. He responded by saying the company would comply with any changes to the law but would not compromise its values.

Cook is now Apple’s official diplomat

Earlier this year, Apple confirmed that Cook’s new role includes responsibility for liaising with governments.

As executive chairman, Cook will assist with certain aspects of the company, including engaging with policymakers around the world.

Attending White House dinner next week

Bloomberg reports that Cook will be attending a White House state dinner for China’s president next week. The event takes place at a difficult time for US-China relations, especially over AI.

Apple Inc. Executive Chairman Tim Cook and OpenAI Chief Executive Officer Sam Altman are poised to attend a White House state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping next week […] The summit comes at a delicate moment for US-Chinese relations — and the artificial intelligence industry. Geopolitical tensions are simmering over the AI race, international trade and the Middle East.

9to5Mac’s Take

I would wager a large sum of money that the idea of the diplomatic role being Cook’s responsibility came from the man himself. It’s a self-sacrificing move intended to free his successor from unnecessary distractions and controversies.

Ternus will of course still be constrained in what he can say when it comes to Apple’s response to controversial policies and laws, whether in the US, China or elsewhere, but having official responses be the responsibility of someone else does give him more latitude than would otherwise be the case.

title: Google Home just became a power user’s paradise
snippet: Good morning. Today I’m finding some peace playing Lumines Remastered, deciding whether to get my kids one of the new 4th-gen Yoto players, and trying to figure out why everyone is freaking out about this recent Tom Cruise interview. more…
fullText:
Good morning. Today I’m finding some peace playing Lumines Remastered, deciding whether to get my kids one of the new 4th-gen Yoto players, and trying to figure out why everyone is freaking out about this recent Tom Cruise interview.

As a reminder, Inbox is the tech newsletter that goes beyond the news cycle. We cover the most important 9to5Google stories from the last couple of days along with a few highlights from around the web. We publish every Tuesday and Thursday, and if you like what you read, please subscribe.

Inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous issues here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column published every Sunday.

⭐️ Starred

Over the past few months, I’ve been using MCP (Model Context Protocol) to connect with my bank, my to-do app (TickTick), my personal database (Obsidian), and anything else I can get my hands on. I find it intuitive to have a conversation with a chatbot about stacking tasks, performing a complex set of calculations, or just figuring out the answer to a difficult problem. 

	

Now Google is getting in on the MCP action with Home MCP, a way to connect coding agents like Claude, Codex, Antigravity, Hermes, and OpenClaw to Google’s Home ecosystem and the products connected to it.

Right now, the tool is limited to Google Home Premium Advanced subscribers in the US, but it’s an ambitious first step toward making it easier to interact with what is usually a digital rat’s nest of brands, categories, and compatibility layers. Google has already rolled out Gemini for Home in an attempt to make automation more straightforward, but I commend the company for dipping its toe into the DIY space and seeing what happens.

According to Google, MCP “gives your favorite AI agent real-world physical context—allowing it to analyze and answer questions about home activity, summarize camera footage across rooms, manage devices on your behalf, or even create your own smart home dashboards using everyday language.” I’m totally going to use it to teach my Nest Cam Outdoor that the cat who wanders onto my driveway every morning isn’t, in fact, a person. Wish me luck.

✉️ Inbox

GM just found the ‘sweet spot’ for supporting Android Auto & CarPlay. See, all it took was people loudly complaining for three years.

MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro goes official with 2nm process and performance gains.

Oppo confirms global Find X10 Pro Max launch powered by MediaTek’s latest flagship chip.

SwiftKey ‘AI voice’ is Pixel 11’s Rambler voice-to-text for other Android phones, works offline. I have my doubts that this is any good — SwiftKey’s been awful for years — but I guess it’s good that this exists?

Google just shared these fun Pixel 11 blueprint wallpapers. These are really fun.

Samsung Gallery is adding Google Photos backup to replace OneDrive. Good, no one uses OneDrive anyway.

Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking powers Gemini Live, Gmail, & Keep. Google is the undisputed leader of text-to-speech, and Gemini 3.8 Live just extends its lead.

The new Boox e-ink devices get Android 16 out of the box, including Palma 3. The Palma 3 looks like an actual gadget, no longer a plastic toy like the previous ones, and I must have it.

Google confirms Pixel phones were exploited in ‘targeted’ attack related to modem. This is pretty concerning, especially because it was “zero-click,” but glad it’s been fixed.

Philips Hue Bridge Pro is now $139, with even bigger price hikes globally. Woof.

Today in bug fixes:

YouTube’s login-breaking bug is getting a fix on TVs and consoles.

Amazon fixes bug that caused problems with Fire TV app sideloading.

🍎 Roll call

It’s iPhone review season, and because this seems like an “S” year, the camera is rightfully getting the most attention. That’s why I watched basically every second of all the new iPhone 18 Pro reviews from channels like PetaPixel, Tyler Stalman, The Verge, and Matti Haapoja.

I’m still not sure what to think about the aperture control. Most reviews are saying that it has very little real-world utility, while others are claiming that it was the only way to offer an f/1.48 lens without sacrificing depth control (or overly relying on software bokeh). Either way, once Apple decides to offer a hardware feature it tends to stick around whether or not it’s any good (see Camera Control), so we’ll likely see a few more generations of this tech.

Sticking with the iPhone theme, two of my favorite podcasters convened this week to discuss the iPhone Duo and how it fares next to the multitude of Android competitors. 

(And if you enjoy the conversation with Stephen Radochia and want to hear more from him, he and I host a little podcast called Old’s Cool that looks at new tech from a vintage point of view.)

➡️ FWD:

This section has some of our favorite stuff from around the internet. Great videos, weird memes, fun reads, recommended apps, whatever. Send us your recommendations!

Tired of getting recorded against your will by other meeting attendees? Kalypta from Deveillance reportedly makes you “inaudible to AI” by “reshaping audio in real time” on your local machine. What a crazy world we live in.

OpenAI’s “Project Lily” tasks real humans with reading ChatGPT transcripts in order to make inference better and more accurate. According to 404 Media, which broke the story, “OpenAI is hiring hundreds of contractors who read a massive stream of real users’ ChatGPT prompts, with the prompts sometimes including sensitive personal information.” 

Snap finally let people try its $2,200 Specs smart glasses, a bulky and unwieldy computer that it’s inviting developers to test. The gadget has a 4-hour battery and can run real apps like Spotify while relying on a proactive AI assistant to do everything else. 

🤑 Action Items

Over the past couple of days, I’ve been trying out a new launcher on my Fold 8, a launcher unlike anything I’ve used on Android before. That’s because it’s defined by its adherence to the UX found on iOS — specifically the upcoming iPhone Duo.

From the demented mind of Reddit’s u/wolftech029, Folio is a love letter (for better or worse) to the way Apple’s home screen drastically differs from the ones found on various Android phones. From predefined grids to Apple’s App Library to the Duo’s funky blur effect, Folio has it all. 

I’m not sure it’s going to stay on my phone for long, but its existence (and the speed at which it was vibe-coded) is a testament to Android’s versatility and openness.

title: Bose Just Dropped New Sport Open Earbuds and Ultra Open Earbuds (2nd Gen)
snippet: Bose’s upgraded $299 top-of-the-line open buds feature improved sound and battery life, while the totally new $199 Sport Open Earbuds are designed for active use.
fullText:
Bose’s original Ultra Open Earbuds were released more than two years ago and sparked the proliferation of a new style of open earbuds that resemble clip-on earrings. I’d been waiting for the Ultra Open Earbuds (2nd Gen) to arrive, and now they’re finally here, with improved sound, voice-calling performance and battery life, Bose says. 

While the updated buds carry the same elevated $299 list price as their predecessor, the company has also unveiled its completely new Sport Open Earbuds that cost $199 and have a different design than the original Ultra Open Earbuds. Both new buds are available for preorder Sept. 19 and ship Oct. 1.

Read more: Best Clip-On Earbuds of 2026

According to Bose, the Ultra Open Earbuds (2nd Gen) feature new drivers, allowing them to play louder and deliver deeper bass. Like Bose’s QuietComfort Ultra Earbuds (2nd Gen), as well as its QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) and QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen), they’re also equipped with the company’s TrueSpatial technology with head-tracking for Immersive Audio, which now includes a Cinema mode. They look very similar to the original, with a slightly upgraded version of the original’s “cuff-clip form factor” that a lot of other people found quite comfortable.

Bose

Available in black, white smoke and “limited-edition” cherry chocolate or olive green colors, they have an IPX4 rating (splash-resistant) and are rated for up to 9 hours of battery life (that’s up from 7 hours), though that number drops if you engage Immersive Audio. 

Thanks to their secure fit and open design, the Ultra Open Earbuds worked well for running and biking, and the new version is also suitable for sporting activities, though Bose is billing the lighter Sport Open Earbuds as more durable and “purpose-built for active use,” with an even more secure fit.

Bose Sport Open Earbuds highlights 

The Sport Open Earbuds look similar to Shokz OpenDots 2 earbuds, which also sell for $199. Bose says they “combine a secure cuff-style fit with soft silicone construction, IP54 sweat, splash and dust resistance, tactile controls and rich open audio, all while keeping listeners naturally aware of their surroundings.”

The Bose Sport Open Earbuds have an IP54 rating and come in three color options.Bose

The Sport Open Earbuds don’t support Bose’s Immersive Audio feature and are rated for up to 7 hours of battery life. They’re available in three colors: black, white smoke and “limited-edition” eucalyptus green (that same color is available for Bose’s recently released QuietComfort (2nd Gen) headphones).

My quick take

I haven’t tried the new buds yet, but I’ll be receiving review samples in advance of their Oct. 1 ship date and will post full hands-on reviews of them.

A lot has changed in the clip-on earbuds market since Bose first released the Ultra Open Earbuds in February 2024, with dozens of new clip-on models available, many of them at far lower prices than $300. While I suspect the Ultra Open Earbuds (2nd Gen) will be among the best-sounding open earbuds and certainly a good premium option in the category, I also think we’ll see these buds on sale fairly frequently; $300 just seems too high to pay for a pair of clip-on earbuds. (Apple’s new AirPods 5 don’t fit as securely as either of these open buds, but they do feature active noise canceling and start at $129.)

The Sport Open Earbuds have a lightweight cuff-clip form factor.Bose

As for the Sport Open Earbuds, I’ll see how they compare to the Shokz OpenDots 2, Anker Aero Clip 2 and Baseus’ XC1 clip-on earbuds ($100), which feature Sound by Bose. Like the Ultra Open Earbuds (2nd Gen), I also expect the Sport Open Buds to see regular discounts to compete with all the new premium sport clip-on buds hitting the market, many of which feature improved sound and voice-calling performance.

title: iOS 27.2 references new option to overwrite iPhone storage with blank data after erasing
snippet: Apple is working on a new option to more thoroughly wipe an iPhone’s storage when erasing the device, but there’s a catch. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple is working on a new option to more thoroughly wipe an iPhone’s storage when erasing the device, but there’s a catch. Here are the details.

New feature exclusive to Chinese devices

References included in today’s iOS 27.2 beta 1 point to a new iPhone erasing option that will let the user overwrite the device’s entire storage with blank data, including storage that isn’t actively in use.

In addition to erasing the iPhone’s data, the feature can overwrite the device’s entire storage with blank data, including storage that isn’t actively in use. Apple warns that the process may take longer than a standard erase and could affect the device’s lifespan.

The move is interesting, as currently, when a user erases an iPhone, the device’s encryption keys are destroyed, effectively rendering the remaining data inaccessible. In fact, Apple is very clear about this in an Apple Platform Deployment support article:

On the device, erasing (or wiping) obliterates all the keys in effaceable storage and renders all user data cryptographically inaccessible.

While digging through today’s beta, 9to5Mac confirmed that, as currently implemented, the feature will only be available on iPhone models sold in China, where Apple appears to be adding it to comply with an upcoming data-erasure requirement.

That’s because a new Chinese standard taking effect on January 1, 2027, will require smartphones and other electronic devices to offer a way to more thoroughly erase stored data, including through methods such as overwriting it.

For semiconductor storage, such as the flash storage used in smartphones, one approved method involves overwriting storage containing user data at least once with meaningless data. That closely matches Apple’s description of replacing storage with blank data.

Finally, the new erasing option won’t be exclusive to iPhones, as code references also point to support for other devices, including the iPad, HomePod, and Apple Vision Pro.

To learn more about China’s upcoming GB 46864-2025 standard, follow this link.

title: X and SpaceXAI move to drop Apple from antitrust lawsuit, keep claims against OpenAI
snippet: X and SpaceXAI today filed a motion to voluntarily dismiss their claims against Apple in the antitrust lawsuit they brought against the company and OpenAI. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
X and SpaceXAI today filed a motion to voluntarily dismiss their claims against Apple in the antitrust lawsuit they brought against the company and OpenAI. Here are the details.

Claims against Apple dropped, pending court approval

Last year, Elon Musk accused Apple and OpenAI of colluding to keep competing AI apps from gaining visibility on the App Store.

Soon after, X and xAI (now, SpaceXAI) filed an antitrust lawsuit against both companies, arguing that Apple’s agreement to integrate ChatGPT into Siri and Apple Intelligence gave OpenAI an unfair advantage over rival AI services. Both companies disputed all claims.

Since then, the case has moved into discovery, with the parties fighting over access to internal documents and communications.

A few months ago, a federal judge ordered Musk to turn over potentially relevant emails from his Tesla and SpaceX accounts after OpenAI argued that he had used those accounts to conduct xAI business.

Today, X and SpaceXAI filed a motion to voluntarily dismiss with prejudice their claims against Apple, while keeping their claims against OpenAI.

From the filing:

Plaintiffs have resolved their claims in this Action against Defendant Apple Inc. (“Apple”).

Plaintiffs accordingly move under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 41(a)(2) to dismiss with prejudice their claims against Apple. Apple does not oppose this Motion.

For the avoidance of doubt, Plaintiffs do not seek to dismiss any of their claims against Defendants OpenAl Foundation (f/k/a OpenAl, Inc.); OpenAl, L.L.C.; and OpenAI OpCo, LLC.

Since X and SpaceXAI moved to dismiss with prejudice their claims against Apple, this means that X and SpaceXAI don’t intend to bring those same claims against Apple again in the future. It is worth mentioning that the dismissal is not final yet, as Judge Mark Pittman still needs to approve it.

As for OpenAI, the case now looks somewhat like a spiritual successor to Musk’s separate lawsuit against the company, Sam Altman, Greg Brockman, and Microsoft, which ended earlier this year.

In that case, Musk accused OpenAI of abandoning the nonprofit mission under which it was founded and improperly enriching its executives at his expense. A jury ultimately rejected Musk’s claims in May, finding that they had been filed too late.⁠

title: iOS 27 adds three new iPhone features you’ll use all the time
snippet: iOS 27 launched this week as a major iPhone update, here are three new features that could be among the most-used for many users. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 launched this week as a major iPhone update, here are three new features that could be among the most-used for many users.

#1: Siri AI

Whatever your opinion of Siri has been in the past, iOS 27’s Siri AI is different.

Siri didn’t just get an AI glow-up with a few upgrades. Apple says it “tore [Siri] to the ground” and “rebuilt it from the ground up.”

You can now ask Siri about anything, like you might ask Google or ChatGPT, and it provides informed, helpful answers. It can also perform way more actions on your iPhone than before, and works seamlessly and consistently across all your devices. There’s also a dedicated Siri app to hold all your conversations.

I’ve been using iOS 27’s new Siri for three full months, and it’s became a daily go-to for me.

#2: Automatic proofreading, including for grammar

The iPhone has long offered a basic spellcheck feature that underlines any words it identifies as misspelled. Now in iOS 27, Apple is expanding proofreading in two ways:

spellcheck is now powered by Apple Intelligence  

there’s a new tool for checking grammar

AI being applied to spellcheck means even if a word is technically spelled correctly, you’ll see suggested word replacements if your iPhone thinks the word is being used incorrectly.

Whereas misspellings are typically underlined in red, suggested word replacements and grammar issues are underlined in blue. Compared to common typos, this makes them feel more like optional suggestions rather than in-your-face warning signs.

If you’re not a fan, you can always disable proofreading in Settings. But I’d guess that for lots of users, these features will be welcome iOS 27 additions.

#3: Search overhaul in Spotlight, Photos, and Mail

Search is one of the most essential features for most apps, and certainly for the iPhone as a whole. And in iOS 27, Spotlight search has received a major overhaul.

In addition to having Siri fully integrated with Spotlight, the iPhone’s systemwide search has been rebuilt with a more comprehensive index of your content that always stays up to date throughout the day.

This means you should find Spotlight more useful than ever, as it offers better and more relevant results with every search. Apple says that the same new search foundation powering Spotlight has been implemented in the Photos and Mail apps too, upgrading search across those key apps. So far in my testing, I can very much tell the difference.

title: DoorDash Can Now Deliver Your Ginormous Costco Order the Same Day
snippet: Uber Eats also expanded its Costco delivery service from 17 states to 47.
fullText:
Ready to get your 1-gallon jug of ketchup and 12-month supply of toilet paper delivered to your door? 

Starting Thursday, DoorDash will offer same-day delivery from every Costco warehouse in the US, the online delivery service said. The announcement comes a day after Uber Eats said it was expanding its Costco delivery from 17 states to 47. DoorDash customers need to have a Costco membership, which costs $65 for the Gold Star plan and $135 for the Executive plan. 

To get started in the DoorDash app, search for Costco and select your local warehouse. Then link the Costco membership and complete the order. The process is basically the same for Uber Eats users.

DoorDash said “groceries, pantry staples, household essentials, electronics, seasonal merchandise, Kirkland Signature products and more” will be available for delivery. Delivery fees will vary, depending on the order, and DashPass members will get free delivery on eligible orders.

Costco has had a delivery partnership with Instacart since 2013. Instacart users don’t need a Costco membership, though they’ll likely pay higher prices than members.

Read more: The 9 Best Grocery Delivery Services of 2026

DoorDash was already delivering Costco products in Australia, New Zealand, Sweden, Iceland and Puerto Rico, and the company added the US to the list after seeing that “Costco” was among the most-searched retailers by app users.

Online grocery delivery trends

Online grocery delivery has been growing fast in recent years. Peapod, HomeGrocer and Webvan tried and failed in the early years of the dot-com boom, partly because of slow internet speeds and high infrastructure costs. But the COVID pandemic triggered a massive surge in the e-grocery business. 

After the nationwide lockdown started in early 2020, monthly online grocery sales in the US jumped to $6.5 billion, up from $2 billion before the pandemic. More than 57% of US households bought groceries online, compared to 25% prior to the lockdown.

Though many returned to brick-and-mortar stores, online grocery shopping has started to pick up again, thanks to deliveries that are faster and more streamlined than ever. Some items from Amazon come in 30 minutes or less, and Walmart also offers half-hour delivery in several US markets. Gopuff delivers convenience items such as snacks, drinks and cleaning products, with thousands in as fast as 15 minutes.

Online grocery sales increased more than 20% year over year for six consecutive quarters through March of this year.

Many US households are also turning more to Costco (and Walmart) as prices continue to rise for groceries, electronics, gas and pretty much everything else. Market research firm Placer.ai said trips to Costco are up by more than 18% since 2019, and Consumer Reports rated Costco and Walmart as offering the best value for groceries.

Concern for Dashers

The DoorDash-Costco partnership is a great new opportunity for delivery workers, but both companies have to make it a win-win for drivers, says Peter Schlactus, co-founder and executive director of the Association for Delivery Drivers. A4DD provides safety training, discounted gear and insurance, and job opportunities for members.

“DoorDash and Costco should together ensure that driver treatment and working conditions meet the highest standards, enabling dedicated drivers to support themselves comfortably as they deserve,” Schlactus told CNET. 

“In their haste to recruit drivers, many gig apps minimize what they ask of drivers and safety training is often a casualty. This puts both drivers and the public at risk, especially given the time pressures that this work entails.”

According to the company’s website, DoorDash drivers (called “Dashers”) receive 100% of all customer tips, including those earned on DoorDash Drive orders.

title: Report: Apple leads slowing true wireless stereo market as open-ear earbuds gain ground
snippet: Apple reportedly maintained its lead in the global true wireless stereo (TWS) market and saw modest year-over-year growth, even as overall shipments declined. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple reportedly maintained its lead in the global true wireless stereo (TWS) market and saw modest year-over-year growth, even as overall shipments declined. Here are the details.

Open wireless stereo shipments counter true wireless stereo slowdown

According to a new report from Omdia (via MacMagazine), Apple shipped 16.8 million TWS devices during the second quarter of 2026, a 1.2% increase from the same period in 2025.

Despite the modest growth, Apple still outperformed the broader market, which declined 0.7% year over year.

Apple’s shipments amounted to 20.5% of the total TWS market for the period, nearly doubling Xiaomi’s 10.4% share in second place. Samsung came in third at 6.7%, followed by Huawei at 6.2%, and OPPO at 5.0%.

Other than Apple, OPPO was the only top-five vendor to see shipment growth. The figure, which includes devices from OnePlus, rose 14.9% year over year.

Interestingly, Omdia also reported worldwide shipments of open wireless stereo (OWS) devices, a subset of TWS devices.

Essentially, Omdia separates conventional TWS products, including in-ear and semi-in-ear earbuds, from OWS devices such as clip-on and ear-hook models that leave the ear canal open.

Omdia says the OWS market saw shipments grow 12% for the period, with Shokz taking the lead at 1.1 million units shipped, representing a 10.3% market share and 107.9% year-over-year growth.

During its “Surprise and Shine” event earlier this month, Apple’s VP of Hardware Engineering, Dave Pakula, referred to the new AirPods 5 as the company’s “beloved open-ear fit,” adding moments later that “AirPods 5 deliver the industry’s best ANC in an open-ear design.” Still, it appears Omdia did not consider the non-Pro AirPods part of the OWS market.

Back to Omdia’s worldwide OWS shipments ranking, Sanag followed Shokz with a 7.6% share and 2.4% year-over-year growth, while Huawei came in third with a 7.0% share despite shipments declining 4.1%. Baseus ranked fourth with 6.6% share and 29.9% growth, followed by Edifier at 5.4% share and 0.2% growth.

Commenting on the results, Omdia said:

Omdia expects OWS to remain one of the most promising growth areas within TWS over the coming years. Annual OWS shipments are forecast to increase from 43.9 million units in 2026 to 90.5 million units by 2030, representing nearly one in five TWS shipments.

title: Google Home app brings battery-efficient widget, reduces gray device tiles
snippet: Besides Home MCP, Google today is also rolling out Home app (especially for the homescreen widget) and Gemini for Home voice assistant updates. more…
fullText:
Besides Home MCP, Google today is also rolling out Home app (especially for the homescreen widget) and Gemini for Home voice assistant updates.

The Google Home widget has now been optimized to “pause background updates and polling whenever your phone’s screen is powered off, locked, or running a screensaver.” This helps save battery on your phone and connected cameras, while “ensuring your widgets refresh immediately the moment you unlock your phone.”

Meanwhile, Google has resolved an issue with device tiles for sensors, cameras, and smoke and carbon monoxide detectors. They could previously “appear grayed out after returning from device controller screens.” As such, you no longer have to reload the screen.

Other quality improvements include:

	

Smoother multi-account switching: If you have multiple accounts that you use with Google Home, switching between them is now more reliable with fewer “Home not found” errors and preference resets.

More reliable smart device setup: Addressed several setup and onboarding issues, including eliminating stalls during Wi-Fi pairing. This ensures a smoother, frustration-free onboarding journey when adding new smart devices to your home.

Smoother Google TV startup: Resolved a startup crash on Google TV devices, ensuring the Google Home experience launches reliably on your television.

More flexible in-app banners: Improved UI for triggering actions in announcement banners in the Google Home app.

Smoke alarm notifications: Rolling out improvements to smoke and carbon monoxide alarm notifications to show current device status in the Google Home app after an alarm has already been cleared.

On the camera front, there are three fixes:

Improved camera live stream tile reliability (Android): Resolved an issue where returning from the full-screen camera view back to the Favorites tab caused live stream tiles to temporarily turn black until manually scrolled. Live feeds now continue streaming seamlessly upon navigating back.

Smoother camera history scrolling across recording gaps (Android): Video timeline scrolling now smoothly scrolls past unrecorded or offline gaps without freezing.

Faster switching to live camera stream (iOS): Fixed an issue where tapping the “Live” button while watching recorded events failed to redirect smoothly into the live view, leaving playback paused.

Finally for September 16, 2026, Google has five Gemini for Home voice assistant updates:

Improved follow up question behavior: Minimized cases where Gemini asks unnecessary follow-up questions or ends conversations awkwardly.

Fixed TV streaming playback: Fixed an intermittent issue that prevented Gemini from launching TV streaming providers on smart displays.

Reduced Live Mode interruptions: Addressed an issue where some devices interrupted themselves during Live Mode.

Reduced Broadcast errors: Resolved an issue where there were error messages when attempting to broadcast. You can now more reliably broadcast across your whole Home.

Improved Playlist reliability: Fixed some issues where Gemini wasn’t able to identify and play personal playlists.

title: Apple Weather adds two convenient new features in iOS 27
snippet: Apple Weather adds two convenient features in iOS 27 that make it easier to track rain and wind forecasts. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Apple Weather adds two convenient features in iOS 27 that make it easier to track rain and wind forecasts. Here are the details.

iOS 27‘s Weather app adds rain and wind forecast views to home page

iOS 27 is packed with new features for Apple Wallet, Calendar, Notes, Messages, and more.

Rain forecast view

Wind forecast view

We’re all familiar with the default forecast view in the Weather app. It’s one of the first things you see every time you open the app.

In iOS 27, Apple has split the forecast view into three options: Conditions, Precipitation, and Wind.

Conditions is the same view that was there before. But now, you can tap the new rain and wind icons to switch to Precipitation and Wind views.

The Precipitation view offers the chance of rain for each hour coming up, plus chances of rain with helpful measurements and time-of-day estimates for the next 10 days. Similarly, the Wind view shows the speed of gusts per hour, and ranges of what to expect in the days ahead.

I’ve been loving these changes during my time using iOS 27. They make key information more accessible than before while letting you stay in the familiar environment of the home screen.

fullText:
It was already clear that Samsung was worried about the impact of the iPhone Duo on its foldable phone range, and there’s now further evidence of the Korean company’s concern.

A blogger who aggregates reports from Chinese social media says there are signs that the company is bringing forward the launch of its Galaxy Z Trifold 2, despite the seeming failure of its predecessor …

Given Samsung’s poor track record on the robustness and reliability of its foldable phones, it’s not surprising that it felt threatened by the build quality of the iPhone Duo. Even before the new model was officially unveiled, the company was criticizing the reported weight of the device.

Once it was announced, it was clear that Apple had addressed a key weakness of Samsung’s foldables: vulnerability to damage caused by the ingress of dust and dirt. While Samsung’s latest folding model is only rated to IP48, leaving it vulnerable to particles as large as a grain of sand, the iPhone Duo is rated to IP68, meaning fully dustproof.

Samsung now appears to be hoping that if one fold isn’t enough, perhaps two will do the trick. Our sister site 9to5Google spotted a report suggesting Samsung plans to bring forward the launch of the Galaxy Z Trifold 2 in direct response to the iPhone Duo.

This would be a more surprising move given that the original dual-fold model wasn’t exactly a market or financial success.

The original TriFold made its US debut in January for $2,900 and was discontinued barely three months later [amid] rumors that it was sold at a loss.

Next year’s model is expected to sell for roughly the same price as the original.

title: Judge rejects OpenAI’s bid to see X’s confidential settlement with Apple in antitrust lawsuit
snippet: Judge Mark Pittman today rejected OpenAI’s request to obtain X and SpaceXAI’s confidential settlement agreement with Apple in their ongoing antitrust case. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Judge Mark Pittman today rejected OpenAI’s request to obtain X and SpaceXAI’s confidential settlement agreement with Apple in their ongoing antitrust case. Here are the details.

Judge says terms aren’t relevant to the remaining case against OpenAI

A few days ago, X and SpaceXAI informed the federal court overseeing their antitrust lawsuit against Apple and OpenAI that, after reaching an agreement with Apple, they would move to dismiss their claims against the iPhone maker.

In the lawsuit, Elon Musk’s companies accused Apple and OpenAI of colluding to shut competing AI apps out of the market, including by preventing them from gaining visibility on the App Store, allegations both companies denied.

After X and SpaceXAI informed the court of the agreement, OpenAI filed an emergency motion asking the judge to compel them to produce its terms, arguing that they could contain information relevant to its defense as the lawsuit continues solely against OpenAI.

Judge Pittman then ordered X and SpaceXAI to submit the agreement privately to the court so he could assess whether it contained information relevant to the remaining case against OpenAI.

Today, he issued his decision, saying that after reviewing the agreement, he found that it does “not present information relevant to the issues” at hand.

From the decision:

The Court hesitates to compel the production of confidential settlement agreements entered by parties. […] Courts have, at times, permitted the production of confidential settlement agreements to the extent they contain information relevant to specific issues at summary judgment or trial. Having conducted an in camera review of the requested materials, however, the Court finds that they do not present information relevant to the issues to be decided at summary judgment or trial in this case.

In his decision, Judge Pittman also notes that OpenAI plans to file a motion for summary judgment (meaning it will ask the court to rule on the case or some of its claims without a trial), and that the court has granted the company additional time to prepare it.

title: MediaTek Dimensity 9600 Pro goes official with 2nm process and performance gains
snippet: MediaTek has unveiled its latest flagship chipset in the Dimensity 9600 Pro, a chip built on TSMC’s latest 2nm process. more…
fullText:
MediaTek has unveiled its latest flagship chipset in the Dimensity 9600 Pro, a chip built on TSMC’s latest 2nm process.

The Dimensity 9600 Pro has a 2+3+3 All Big Core CPU design using Arm’s new C2-Ultra cores at 4.55GHz, three C2-Pro cores at 4.35GHz, and three more C2-Pro cores at 3.1GHz. Altogether, MediaTek says that its latest design delivers 17% better single-core performance and 15% higher multi-core performance compared to last year’s chip. 

Leading where others follow, the MediaTek Dimensity 9600 is a first-wave 2nm smartphone chip design that’s built to simultaneously raise the bar on performance, capability, and power-efficiency…

At its heart is MediaTek’s 4th-generation All Big Core CPU: a revolutionary 2+3+3 design pairing two Arm C2-Ultra processors, three Arm C2-Pro processors with 1MB L2 cache and three Arm C2-Pro with 512KB L2 cache, which altogether contribute to a 21% larger L2 cache system.

…MediaTek leads the industry with first-wave support for both UFS 5.0, which delivers 2x faster read/writes than the previous generation, and LPDDR6, which boosts effective memory bandwidth by 33% at the same frequency.

This latest chip adopts LPDDR6 memory and UFS 5.0 storage. The G2-Ultra NX GPU brings a 27% boost to peak performance while hitting 24% lower power consumption. Ray-tracing is 18% faster and games support up to 185fps. 

On the AI side, Dimensity 9600 Pro’s second-gen Super Efficient NPU reduces power consumption by 40% while delivering better performance and higher token generation per watt. 

	

Rounding things out, the Imagiq 1290 ISP supports 4K240 native direct-output ultra-slow-motion video, 4K120 cinematic log, and AI-powered True Color Tone and 60fps motion capture features. 

One of the first devices powered by the Dimensity 9600 Pro will be Oppo’s Find X10 Pro Max, due to be announced next week. Meanwhile, MediaTek is also announcing the Dimensity 9600M as a lower-cost version of this chip with “flagship-level performance.” It lacks UFS 5.0 and uses Arm’s C1 cores instead of C2.

fullText:
Apple may still be cleaning up after the end of the iPhone launch, but attention is already turning to an October event.

There are still a lot of new products we’re expecting the company to unveil, with the most exciting of these including touchscreen MacBooks and a smart home hub we’ve been dubbing the HomePad. But which ones will launch this year, and which ones will have to wait until next year … ?

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman has laid out his latest expectations. He’s still being a little coy with exact timings, simply saying that some products will launch “later this year” rather than specifically in an October event. That could potentially allow for some launches next month and others closer to the end of the year.

This year

Gurman says we can expect six new products later this year:

Touchscreen MacBook Pro models (likely in 14- and 16-inch versions)

An updated 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M6 chip (non-touchscreen model)

A new iMac, although this will only be new colors and an M6 processor

HomePod mini 2, with Siri AI

Apple TV 4K, with Siri AI

iPad mini, with OLED screen

However, he still has no answer on whether we can expect to see the launch of the HomePad, stating that while it may launch in October, the timeline is “likely still fluid.”

First half of 2027

The iPhone Air 2 is potentially the most significant of the product launches expected in the first half of next year. This is expected to add an ultrawide camera and to offer improved battery life. The iPad Air is also expected to get an OLED screen for the first time, as well as a more powerful chip.

The rest of the list is lengthy, but mostly comprises iterative updates:

IPhone 18, mostly expected to be the iPhone 17 with A20 chip

Smart glasses; AirPods with built-in cameras; a home security system and related device; a redesigned Apple Watch; a 20th-anniversary iPhone line; and a second-generation iPhone Duo.

snippet: Following an extended beta period, Android 17 QPR1 is rolling out to Google Pixel devices with the September 2026 Feature Drop and security patch. more…
fullText:
Following an extended beta period, Android 17 QPR1 is rolling out to Google Pixel devices with the September 2026 Feature Drop and security patch.

There are a number of interface changes in Android 17 QPR1, starting with more blur effects across the system UI. The volume panel is where you’ll most likely notice the Dynamic Color-themed translucency, with the full bottom sheet also updated. The Power menu has also been refreshed and is joined by a background blur. This matches the updates that the widgets picker received in the initial Android 17 June release.

The system media player has a new Material 3 carousel-based interface when there are multiple apps. Instead of dots at the bottom, you now see a preview of other open applications, with your current card shrinking to make room.

When opening Quick Settings, you’ll notice a new bouncy animation, while there’s a new icon in the bottom-right corner for making edits.

	

The Mobile Data Tile has been updated with a “Don’t ask me again” toggle. There’s also a new QS Tile for “Keyboard” that lets you access the system switcher. The Screen recording tool now defaults to the last-used application.

When long-pressing on homescreen apps, the menu has been split into app Shortcuts and system Actions (like Bubble and Widgets).

Meanwhile, holding down on an empty homescreen spot reveals an updated fast wallpaper switcher that has more pronounced corner rounding, while the gaps between menu items have been removed. Other changes include:

There’s a new M3 Expressive Settings app icon that was first introduced on the Pixel Watch.

New animation when launching the camera from lockscreen with power button double-tap.

Health Connect on phones can now track distance and calories burned in addition to step count.

Android 17 QPR1 is rolling out starting today for the Pixel 6, Pixel 6 Pro, Pixel 6a, Pixel 7, Pixel 7 Pro, Pixel 7a, Pixel Tablet, Pixel Fold, Pixel 8, Pixel 8 Pro, Pixel 8a, Pixel 9, Pixel 9 Pro, Pixel 9 Pro XL, Pixel 9 Pro Fold, Pixel 9a, Pixel 10, Pixel 10 Pro, Pixel 10 Pro XL, Pixel 10 Pro Fold, Pixel 10a, Pixel 11, Pixel 11 Pro, Pixel 11 Pro XL, and Pixel 11 Pro Fold.

Visit Settings > System > System update and click the “Check for update” button if the OTA hasn’t already appeared on your device. Android 17 QPR1 Beta 9 users will get a small update to this final release.

The Android Beta Program will remain open and continue testing QPRs and feature drops. 

To get the stable version, those running the Android 17 QPR1 Beta have to opt out first. Devices will not be wiped by the stable OTA once that becomes widely available.

title: Amazon fixes bug that caused problems with Fire TV app sideloading [U]
snippet: Fire TV hardware will be able to freely sideload apps again without issue after an upcoming Android software update for Amazon’s streaming hardware. more…
fullText:
Fire TV hardware will be able to freely sideload apps again without issue after an upcoming Android software update for Amazon’s streaming hardware.

Late last year, Amazon rolled out a series of software patches to its Fire TV hardware. On the surface, the Android update for the streaming devices contained the usual security patches and performance updates. It was later discovered that the update also seemed to disable sideloading on certain Fire TV devices, preventing third-party apps from being installed if they didn’t come from certified app stores.

Amazon recently commented on that aspect of its previous Android updates in a response to AFTV News. Amazon says sideload prevention was due to a bug in the update and wasn’t an intentional part of the patch.

If users attempted to install a third-party app, the Fire TV device would list an error and block the process in some instances. It didn’t appear to affect all Fire TV devices, though the issue was widespread enough to be considered intentional. According to Amazon, it wasn’t.

	

There was a bug in a recent Fire TV Settings update that caused the “Install unknown apps” list to appear incomplete or empty on some Fire TV devices. We have identified the cause and a fix will roll out in an upcoming Fire TV Settings update, installed automatically on affected devices over the coming week.

This comes as the company recently announced its latest Fire TV Stick, which runs on Vega OS – not Android. It also confirmed that all future Fire TV Stick devices would run Linux-based software in lieu of Google’s OS to achieve a better performance-to-power ratio.

In essence, existing Fire TV devices will seemingly be able to sideload apps again, but that likely won’t be the case for streaming hardware Amazon launches in the future. Amazon says the patch will roll out to affected devices “over the coming week.”

title: YouTube’s login-breaking bug is getting a fix on TVs and consoles
snippet: Users met with an error at login, preventing them from accessing their YouTube account on TVs, and some consoles will be happy to know Google is rolling out a fix. more…
fullText:
Users met with an error at login, preventing them from accessing their YouTube account on TVs, and some consoles will be happy to know Google is rolling out a fix.

An issue began popping up for some users in the last couple of days, preventing a successful login on the TV or console app. Even with the proper password, some users were reporting they were unable to log back in after being kicked out. The issue seemed to persist on Xbox, PlayStation consoles, smart TVs, and streaming hardware – what YouTube classifies as “licing room devices.”

According to YouTube, the login bug that logged users out and blocked them from re-entry has been fixed. YouTube says the issue has been investigated and is now “fully fixed” in a community post separate from existing threads.

It’s unclear when this issue truly began, but there have been several new threads posted on Reddit within the last 24 hours, suggesting the bug affected a wide number of users worldwide.

	

The community post didn’t suggest an app update was needed. It was likely a server-side bug blocking Google Accounts from access, and in some cases, guest accounts.

Did YouTube block you from logging in? Is it fixed for you now?

Good morning. Today I’m wondering if I should revisit Diablo IV in light of the Diablo V announcement, what I would possibly do with a Steam Frame if I could justify its $1,059 price, and whether I missed any major features by reading as many iOS 27 and macOS 27 reviews as I can stomach.

As a reminder, Inbox is the tech newsletter that goes beyond the news cycle. We cover the most important 9to5Google stories from the last couple of days along with a few highlights from around the web. We publish every Tuesday and Thursday, and if you like what you read, please subscribe.

Inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous issues here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column published every Sunday.

⭐️ Starred

We’ve known for years that Apple was building a foldable phone, which means that Samsung, the company that popularized the format, also knew. So in July, when the company unveiled the Galaxy Z Fold 8, a wide foldable with proportions similar to the rumored iPhone Duo, it was seen largely as a preemptive move to claim, once again, that Samsung was ahead of the curve.

	

And thankfully the phone was a success; it sold better than expected, and Samsung has been left scrambling for components from next year’s model to satisfy demand today.

But Samsung, as it is wont to do, couldn’t let the phone’s success just speak. It had to inject itself into the conversation around the iPhone Duo in a series of posts that can only be described as cringe. To me, it’s another case of this “I don’t think about you at all” meme.

Of course, this is just silly stuff, but it speaks to the perception that even when Samsung leads, it follows. The good news is that, as Samsung points out in this funny but awkward ad called “Switchers,” it’s now much easier to move from iPhone to Android since Apple and Google collaborated on a new framework.

Samsung appears to be taking the Duo’s release in stride, doubling down on its commitment to foldables by reportedly moving up the release of its second-generation TriFold.

Apple on wide Android foldables beating iPhone Duo; ‘They got the aspect ratio’

✉️ Inbox

Android rolling out passkey transfers between password managers. It’s no longer difficult to transfer credentials between password managers, but passkeys have always been another matter. This system-level change is more than welcome.

Samsung’s first Android XR glasses with a color display may launch in late 2027. We’re only a month or so away from Samsung’s first smart glasses released in collaboration with Google, Warby Parker, and Gentle Monster, so it’s no surprise that by the end of next year there will be an option with a display.

Google brings Gemini for desktop app to Windows. It feels like it’s been forever since Google announced a Windows version of its popular Gemini app, but it’s now available and appears fully featured.

Google details ADB Wi-Fi 2.0 for more reliable wireless Android debugging

YouTube details NFL Sunday Ticket pricing & availability for 2026 season, including a 50% discount. The absolute disaster that is watching NFL games in one place with one subscription doesn’t appear to be any better for the 26/27 season. 

NFL Sunday Ticket is $204/year for YouTube Premium subscribers, nearly 60% off

Google’s hyper-personalized ‘Dreambeans’ feed is now free to test. I still have no idea what this is; I just know that it has the worst possible name for an app.

The Galaxy Z Fold 8 needs battery banks that actually fit; iPhone Duo might help. One benefit of Apple launching a similarly sized foldable is that accessory makers may unintentionally make things better on the Android side.

Possible Google device at FCC could be Wear OS-powered fitness tracker. It would not surprise me if Google is working on more fitness trackers after the runaway success of the Fitbit Air. Hope this one lacks a screen, too.

Oppo confirms Find X10 series details ahead of September 22 launch. The next Find X flagships are coming soon, and they’re just as ambitious as previous generations.

Googlebook pre-orders start on September 21. I’m waiting with bated breath to see why anyone should care about these laptops, particularly in light of a new slate of very good, relatively inexpensive Windows-powered MacBook Neo competitors.
