Welcome to a new project I’m calling Cc:, where I ask interesting people in the community about what’s making them happy both inside and outside the world of tech. This week, I’m speaking with my friend and former colleague, Nicholas Sutrich.

Who are you?

Nicholas Sutrich

What do you do for work?

I’m the Senior Content Producer at Android Central. This is a fancy title that really means I test a lot of devices every week and write about them.

What do you do for fun?

I reviewed devices for 10 years on the side before going full-time, so I still like to think of my job as being a fun hobby I just so happen to get paid for. Other than work, I love video gaming with my wife and son, reading novels, gardening and chicken tending, CrossFit, and the occasional hike when I can squeeze it in.

What is your relationship like with technology these days?

I spend less time on my phone now than maybe ever. I’ve deleted all social media off my phone (otherwise, I find I work too much for my own good), and I don’t generally play games on my phone unless I’m doing it for a review. My goal is to get off my devices when work is over and spend more quality time with friends and family in person, instead. 

What are a few apps you can’t live without and why?

eMeals: A meal planning service I subscribe to. It’s $5 a month and has a boatload of recipes on there, plus new recipes each week and plans for specific dietary restrictions, stores, or budgets.

Zepp: This is the app for Amazfit smartwatches. I use it for food logging and for workout logging. The food logging portion is particularly fantastic because it’s LLM-driven, so you can tell it you had “2 eggs fried in coconut oil with 2 slices of avocado toast and a glass of orange juice for breakfast” and it’ll log all that crap instantly. No more scrolling through tedious lists.

Discord: Everyone probably uses this, but it’s my main chat app with friends. We bounced between apps for years until it came out and haven’t switched since. 

What is a gadget that you love right now?

Motorola Razr Fold. This phone is just such a joy to use. Excellent camera and displays, never have to worry about battery life. Software is snappy and has great features (double-chop for flashlight, woot!). Oh, and the sides are CURVED, not friggin’ flat. I hate stupid phones with flat sides, especially foldables.

What’s a recent TV show you loved?

Gotta be Pursuit of Jade on Netflix. It’s a time period drama/romance/kung-fu show set in ancient China. We randomly tried it after The Algorithm™️ recommended it to us and haven’t stopped since. We only watch like 20-30 mins of TV a day tops, so it’s taken a while to get through all 40 episodes, especially since they’re usually 45 minutes or so apiece.

What’s a recent book you loved?

Jurassic Park by Michael Crichton. I somehow never read these books (although I love the OG movie). It was fun reading the original content and seeing the author’s direction for the story versus the films. Also fascinating to see what parts of the book the films stripped out and randomly slapped into other movies.

What’s a recent movie you loved?

Project Hail Mary. I read this book twice (one of which was out loud to my family) and was so happy that they were making a movie. It’s such an excellent mix of science reality and science fiction in a unique end-of-times scenario. If aliens exist, I hope they’re like Rocky.

What’s a recent game you loved?

Orbitals for the Nintendo Switch 2. I’ve played many co-op games in my time, but few are as well produced and executed as Orbitals. The visuals are beyond stunning and make you feel like you’re playing a Studio Ghibli movie. It’s basically impossible to describe the gameplay other than a wild mix of adventure, puzzle, and platforming.

What’s something offline you do every day that brings you joy?

Family reading time. We’ve done this since our son was little and it never ceases to be wonderful. At the end of most days (I wish we did it every day), we’ll curl up in bed or on the couch and read together. Sometimes, it’s reading manga; other times, it’s an audiobook or reading aloud to each other. We’ve gone through a lot of books this way, and it’s a great way to spend quality time together, drink some tea, have snacks, and start conversations.

Thank you, Nick, for being awesome as always. See you on the putting green.

Over the weekend, American AI titans, including Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, OpenAI’s Sam Altman, xAI’s Elon Musk, and Google DeepMind’s Demis Hassabis, came out in support of “pacing the frontier,” a term popularized by a letter released in July by nearly 1,400 employees of large American AI companies.

In fact, Amodei wrote his own 3,000+ word paean called “We Must Pace the Frontier,” in which he posits that the industry needs to slow down its frenetic work on improving AI model capabilities in order to prioritize alignment and safety.

“Given the accelerating rate of AI capability development, it’s my worry that in 6–12 months such a swarm could be capable of taking over the entire internet with a persistent botnet (potentially causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage), and that the scale of damage would continue to increase from there if AI becomes more powerful without the necessary guardrails.”

This self-policed slowdown comes as the US government continues to distance itself from regulation, despite entreaties from both sides of the aisle, as well as countries around the world. In a Truth Social post, President Trump said that “the only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades! There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China. WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS! We are leading China, and all others, and will continue to do so.”

title: Roku Just Added More Than 30 Streaming Bundles to Help People Save Money
snippet: Here’s a look at pricing and some of the most enticing packages for HBO Max, Starz, Hallmark Plus and more.
fullText:
In case you missed it, multiple streaming services have increased their prices this year, and a few have joined forces to offer bundles. Roku on Thursday announced the addition of more than 30 bundles for viewers in the US and Mexico, with savings of up to 33% per month depending on which options you sign up for. Howdy, Roku’s own ad-free, $3-per-month streaming service is included in the offerings.

These aren’t limited-time deals, either — customers will find multiple combinations of two streaming services packaged together that include offerings like Starz with AMC Plus, AMC Plus with Hallmark Plus or HBO Max and Cinemax. You can shop for these bundles on your Roku devices, in the phone app or on the web via the Roku Channel. Below is a sampling of the streaming duos available in the US and their monthly prices. If you want to see the full list of bundles, head here, but check the subscriptions section on your Roku device for pricing on every offering. 

HBO Max and Cinemax: $23 per month ($28.48 without bundle)

Starz and MGM Plus: $14 per month ($20 without bundle)

Howdy and Hallmark Plus: $9 per month ($11 without bundle)

Starz and AMC Plus: $16 per month ($23 without bundle)

Starz and Hallmark Plus: $15 per month ($20 without bundle)

Curiosity Stream and Magellan TV: $9 per month ($12 without bundle)

Starz and Crunchyroll: $17 per month ($22 without bundle)

AMC Plus and Hallmark Plus: $14 per month ($19 without bundle)

BritBox and BBC: $14 per month ($18 without bundle)

A&E Crime Central and Howdy: $7 per month ($9 without bundle)

Fox One and Fox Nation: $25 per month ($28 without bundle)

If you already have a subscription to a premium service like Starz or Howdy, it’s possible you can change to one of these bundles without worrying about being billed twice, according to Roku. Customers will only need to cancel their current plan and then switch. The company also said it plans to roll out more streaming bundles in the future.

In more than 100 countries, Apple has launched a new initiative that bundles Apple TV and Apple Arcade subscriptions into iCloud+, at no extra charge. Rather than the pricier Apple One bundles, rolling everything into iCloud+ now seems to be the company’s strategy for services growth in smaller territories and price-sensitive developing markets.

This will clearly boost the access of Apple’s content services in these markets. You can find the full list of over 100 supported countries below, spoiler alert it does not include the United States …

title: The US Military Can’t Stop Talking About Space Weapons
snippet: Three senior military officials have confirmed the US has space weapons this week. Why now?
fullText:
After decades of silence, the US military is suddenly chatty on the topic of space weapons.

Earlier this week, Air Force Secretary Troy Meink revealed at the Air, Space & Cyber Conference in Maryland that the US has fielded “on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the Joint Force against hostile adversary action.” The next day, Chief of Space Operations Gen. Douglas Schiess echoed the same message. 

Two days later, I listened to Gen. Stephen N. Whiting, the commander of the US Space Command, put his own spin on the space weapons announcement during the Advanced Maui Optical and Space Surveillance Technologies Conference.

“The Joint Force retains on-orbit space control weapons fully capable of defending the United States and its interests against hostile adversary actions,” Whiting said. 

Whiting did not elaborate on what those weapons are, if they’d target objects in space or on Earth or how long they’ve been active. 

“We need the ability to affect targets,” he told a group of reporters after his address. “The discussion that we’ve had over the last couple days just highlights that we have those capabilities.”

The idea that the US is fielding space weapons didn’t come as a huge surprise to anyone in the industry. The shock was the timing. Why are Washington’s top commanders suddenly broadcasting the militarization of space this week?

“I still don’t get it. Why now?” said Victoria Samson, chief director of space security and stability, Secure World Foundation. “Russia and China are going to look at this as continued evidence that the US is a bad actor in space. This makes our job of getting international participants to sign on to our vision of responsible behavior in space that much harder.”

I sat down with Whiting and a group of reporters to ask these questions. But like the other commanders discussing space weapons this week, he largely declined to get into specifics.   

Military officials blame China and Russia

In the meeting with reporters after his address, Whiting pointed to China and Russia as the first countries to deploy space weapons. 

“China and Russia have developed and fielded counter-space weapons, the whole range of kinetic and nonkinetic capabilities,” he said. “That is not in doubt, and that has happened.”

Russia used a ground-based missile to blow up one of its own defunct satellites in 2021, an event that created more than 1,500 pieces of debris larger than a softball and likely hundreds of thousands of smaller pieces. China has also deployed similar antisatellite weapons in the past – most notably a 2007 incident that created the largest debris cloud in history. 

While there haven’t been confirmed instances of China and Russia deploying orbital weapons against adversaries, the experts I spoke with at AMOS said aggressive behavior is commonplace, including actions that look like data siphoning from adversary satellites or communications jamming. 

“Between China and Russia on orbit, this is happening all the time,” said Jason Ruggieri, a director at COMSPOC, a company that tracks objects in space. “We can’t make an assessment when they have a close approach with a satellite about what exactly they were doing, but we can make assumptions based on open-source intelligence.”

What do space weapons look like?

When I polled space experts at AMOS about what type of weapon the US military officials are referring to, communications jammers was the most common answer. 

“The Russians and Chinese are thought to have them. It seems pretty obvious,” said Samsen. “Before this, the US had three declared offensive counter-space capabilities — all jammers. Those are like intro to counter-space capabilities or basic stepping stones. So if it was like that on Earth, I don’t know why it wouldn’t be that in space.”

Both China and Russia swiftly condemned the US for escalating tensions in space. 

“We urge the US side to stop expanding its military capabilities and preparing for war in outer space,” Chinese ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said in response to Meink’s comments. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov also called on Tuesday to keep space “free of any weapons.”

Whiting framed this week’s flurry of announcements as the logical conclusion to a decade of militarization in space. 

“Uniformed warfighters have capabilities to be able to defend American interests in their domain. That is not a controversial statement for those who operate in the air or at sea, on the land or in cyber. But it may be a new statement for us in space,” he said. “It is all about normalizing the domain as a place that we defend American interests.’

President Donald Trump has made dominance in space a priority during his second stint in office. On Aug. 20, he set a target of “1,000 launches and reentries every year” by 2030, many of which would deliver military payloads to orbit. For comparison, 2025 saw 193 launches in the US – 85% of which were from SpaceX, according to BryceTech. 

A week after taking office in 2025, Trump also directed the Department of Defense to create a Golden Dome missile defense system using thousands of satellites that would be equipped with orbital weapons. The Congressional Budget Office estimated that it would cost $1.2 trillion to develop and operate over 20 years. 

None of the military officials said what kind of space weapon the US has deployed already, but an official who spoke to The Washington Post on the condition of anonymity said it could be a weapon that would allow the military to take out an enemy’s satellite if it’s being used to target American troops or a US satellite.

“US allies and partners are going to say, ‘Oh, if the US thinks it needs weapons in space, we probably do too.’ And it will proliferate,” Samsen said. “Truly it’ll be an arms race in space.”

title: September 2026 Pixel Drop: VIPs widget redesign, more Pixel Watch gestures
snippet: Google today is rolling out the September 2026 Pixel Drop. This is a smaller update, with Android 17 QPR1 bringing the bulk of new features and changes. That said, recent weeks have seen updates for Pixel Journal, Now Playing, Recorder, Screenshots, and Weather. more…
fullText:
Google today is rolling out the September 2026 Pixel Drop. This is a smaller update, with Android 17 QPR1 bringing the bulk of new features and changes. That said, recent weeks have seen updates for Pixel Journal, Now Playing, Recorder, Screenshots, and Weather.

Phones

Google has redesigned the Pixel VIPs widget to let you quickly call and text contacts with a single tap from your homescreen instead of having to first open the bottom sheet.

A new floating navigation overlay lets you swipe the bottom of your screen to switch between your favorite people. Finally, Pixel VIPs will show glanceable notification badges on the widget. 

This redesign is rolling out for the Pixel 6+ in all regions and languages with version 2.0 of the Pixel VIPs app/service and Google Contacts 4.77+.

	

After introducing on the Pixel 11 series, Pause Point is now coming to the Pixel 6 and newer. This Digital Wellbeing feature “adds a pause before you open a distracting app of your choice.”

Updated: Scam Detection warnings now appear in the Gboard suggestions strip “wherever you chat.” The “Likely scam” warning will appear ”when you start typing a response to a suspicious message.” Available on the Pixel 6+ in the US, processing happens on your device.

Additionally, the existing Scam Detection in notifications is expanding to nine new countries (Australia, Canada, France, Germany, India, Japan, Mexico, Singapore, and the United Kingdom), as well as six new languages (Arabic, French, German, Portuguese, Japanese, and Spanish).

To mark the release of Harry Potter: The Full-Cast Audio Editions, there are three new Pixel Themes. This covers wallpapers, icons, and sounds, with eligible Pixel users also getting a two-month Audible free trial.

Pixel Watch

Owners of the Pixel Watch 3 and 4 can now scroll through their notification tray using the one-handed pinch gesture. This has been quite convenient on the PW5.

Meanwhile, the Pixel Watch 4 receives an updated raise-to-talk model that improves accuracy and performance when activating Gemini.

fullText:
9to5Mac is brought to you by CleanMyMac by MacPaw. With the release of macOS 27 Golden Gate, use CleanMyMac first to free up space, optimize your system, and ensure your new Mac runs at 100% on day one. Learn more.

macOS 27 Golden Gate doesn’t give the Photos app a dramatic redesign. Instead, Photos gains a surprisingly broad set of various improvements this year. These range from Apple Intelligence-powered editing, new ways to organize and sort your collection, better sharing tools, and much more.

More powerful Apple Intelligence editing

The flashiest updates to the Photos app in macOS 27 Golden Gate live in a new Tools pane. They require Apple Intelligence on a compatible Mac.

Clean Up gets a significant quality boost. Apple says it can now handle larger objects and more complex scenes with more realistic results.

Separately, a fast mode is intended for small blemishes, while high quality mode tackles more intricate edits not possible before.

The new Extend tool uses generative models to expand an image beyond its original edges.

That can help when straightening a horizon, changing an aspect ratio, or simply creating more space around a subject. Extend is also available from the Crop tool.

Then there’s Spatial Reframing.

First, Photos builds a 3D view of a scene using on-device spatial models. This lets you rotate around a subject, pan, or zoom to change the apparent camera position.

When the new perspective exposes gaps, image models generate the missing areas.

In macOS 27, iCloud Shared Albums finally support full-resolution sharing and all common photo and video formats.

They’re also becoming much friendlier to people outside the Apple ecosystem. Friends using Android or Windows can join a Shared Album and contribute their own photos through iCloud.com.

Apple is also addressing some everyday friction. You can save every photo from a Shared Album to your personal library with a single click.

For albums that do not need to live forever, there is a new option to have them expire after 30 days.

Slideshows, ratings, and a new collection

Next, Photos is bringing back more control over slideshows. You can turn any selection of photos and videos into a slideshow, then customize its slide duration, transition style, and music.

After that, the finished slideshow can be saved as a video file in your photo library. That makes it much easier to replay or share the presentation without making it again each time.

Additionally, a new Captured by Me collection gathers photos you took with the Camera app, including shots captured on previous devices. The same criteria can also be used as a filter elsewhere in your library.

And photographers who want another way to organize their work, Photos adds one-to-five-star ratings. Ratings can then be used to filter the main library and collections. Just be sure to enable star ratings in Photos app settings as it’s off by default.

Faster uploads and better search

Lastly, two less visible changes could make Photos feel better in daily use.

macOS 27 lets you prioritize iCloud Photos syncing so new photos and videos begin uploading sooner.

This sounds especially useful when you’ve just imported a large batch and want it available on your other devices without waiting for lower-priority work.

Apple has also rebuilt the search foundation used by Spotlight, Photos, and Mail. Apple says the new system creates a more comprehensive index of your content and keeps it updated throughout the day, so that can only be positive.

macOS 27 Golden Gate improves how you share, organize, find, sync, present, and edit your photos. Together, these changes make for a more meaningful year for the app for regular Photos app users.

title: Don’t Skip the iPhone Duo Just Because It’s a First-Generation Phone
snippet: While undeniably pricey, being one of the first to use an iPhone Duo means your voice gets to shape what happens next.
fullText:
Every big purchase in your life is a roll of the dice, but buying the first version of something always feels extra risky. The new iPhone Duo looks cool, with its passport-style hinge and massive displays, but buying it is still a risk. You’re spending at least $2,000 on something you’ll use for multiple hours every day over at least the next 12 months, which is enough to give just about anyone a moment of pause to check in mentally and make sure this is the right decision.

The risk is real, but the rewards could potentially be felt by millions for years to come.

Apple/Screenshot by CNET

Apple is nowhere near the first to make a foldable phone, but this is the first iPhone that will bend (more than once, at least). That’s an interesting place to be, due largely to the folks who tend to own iPhones. Samsung is in its seventh year of releasing foldables, and I maybe see one or two of them in the wild when I wander major cities or busy airports. The folks who have them love them, and they’re happy to tell their friends about the cool things these phones can do, but the audience is largely early adopters, comfortable with things that aren’t fully baked. 

Feedback from someone who isn’t tech-obsessed will always be more valuable to Apple than to a lot of its competitors. Features will be created and retired from that feedback, and it will eventually appear on most other folding phones.

My favorite example of this is actually another Apple product, the Watch. The first Apple Watch had some fitness features, but was largely focused on the idea that you could leave your phone behind because that’s what the competition was doing already. Instead of trying to replicate your phone in watch form, right down to the tiny keyboard seen on other smartwatches at the time, Apple focused on its fitness tracking and health monitoring features. They quickly became the most popular.

By the time the third-gen Apple Watch was announced, GPS and cellular features were now being shown off as a way to make those fitness features better. The Watch was no longer about replacing your phone. Now that we’re at Apple Watch Gen 12, fitness is basically all anyone talks about.

The iPhone Duo can be propped half-open to easily watch movies and access controls.Abrar Al-Heeti/CNET

The next six months are going to be important for the future of Apple’s contribution to the foldable phone market, because the audience response will help shape the next iPhone Duo. Popular third-party apps will become native features, accessories will be made to address situations that haven’t happened yet and current features will be copied in every direction. It benefits everyone if the majority of the folks providing early feedback and getting excited about new ways to use this phone are outside of the standard group of IT folks, business execs on weekly flights or whoever is going to watch that front screen for 44 hours.

Grab one, if you can afford it. Watch Netflix on it and talk about how that experience could be better. Use your favorite apps side by side and see if it’s easy or intuitive for you to figure out on your own. Be an early adopter, and this time next year a lot more people will feel like the Duo was made with them in mind.

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Russell Holly

title: Here’s what’s new with parental control features in iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27
snippet: Included in today’s 2027 system updates from Apple are several new Screen Time and parental control features aimed at giving parents more control over how their kids use their devices. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Included in today’s 2027 system updates from Apple are several new Screen Time and parental control features aimed at giving parents more control over how their kids use their devices. Here are the details.

Today’s updates include important parental control improvements

Apple today released iOS 27, iPadOS 27, and macOS 27 with what it describes as a “new suite of powerful, intuitive, and easy-to-use tools that helps parents create safer digital experiences for their kids,” many of which the company previewed in June, during the WWDC26 keynote.

In essence, the new features focus on four areas: what content kids can access, who they can communicate with, when they can use their devices, and how parents can manage those controls.

All of them fall under the protections and restrictions of Child Accounts, which Apple says are required for children under 13, or the equivalent minimum age in their country or region, and available for children up to 18.

With iOS 27, Apple has also simplified the setup process for new Child Accounts. Parents can start with a small set of essential apps, a recommended starter set, or choose exactly which Apple apps their child can access from the outset.

Once a parent sets up a Child Account, they can choose which apps and websites their child can access, as well as set age and content restrictions for movies, TV shows, music, books, and other media.

Parents can now also rely on Ask to Browse, a feature that lets kids request access to blocked websites in Safari across iPhone, iPad, and Mac, with parents approving requests in Messages. This is similar to Ask to Buy, which already requires parental approval before children can download apps or make in-app purchases.

Parents can also require kids to ask for approval before connecting with new contacts, set shared or individual daily limits for categories such as Entertainment, Games, and Social Media, and create schedules that determine which apps are available at different times of day. Those schedules can also vary depending on the day of the week.

Screen Time itself has also been redesigned, with a new architecture that Apple says makes parental controls sync more quickly across devices in a Family Sharing group. Parents can now see weekly usage summaries and their kids’ most-used apps at a glance, temporarily pause access to a device, open things back up for a limited period, and quickly switch between different schedules.

Communication Safety is also expanding beyond nudity detection. The feature can now block detected gore or violent content in shared images and videos, while displaying a warning and additional resources.

Time Allowances are also more flexible. Parents can create their own app categories, move apps between them, and assign a time allowance as soon as they approve a new app through Ask to Buy. Websites associated with an app can also automatically follow the same allowance.

Apple says its suggested Time Allowances are based on a child’s age and expert research. The company is also working with the American Academy of Pediatrics to adapt its Family Media Plan into guidance for parents using Apple products.

Finally, Apple notes that all devices in a Family Sharing group need to be running the version 27 software releases to use the new Screen Time experience.

title: The iPhone 18 Pro Brings 3 Upgrades That Will Make My Traveling Life So Much Easier
snippet: Commentary: The iPhone 18 Pro seems to fix almost every gripe I’ve had with my iPhone 17 Pro Max — especially for how much I travel.
fullText:
I’ve traveled all over the world with the iPhone 17 Pro Max during the past year, but I think the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max have made the right changes for someone like me who’s constantly on the go. The new Pro phones debuted last week at the company’s  “Surprise and Shine” event, and I think three new features in particular will solve the gripes I’ve had with my orange 17 Pro Max as a traveling companion.

While I am in awe of the Ceramic Shield 2 durability that impressively protected my screen, I wouldn’t call it the best travel phone. It gets warm to the touch in hot weather and doesn’t offer the same pleasing camera experience as Android heavyweights like the Vivo X300 Ultra, Xiaomi 17 Ultra or the Oppo Find X9 Ultra. That’s why I’m stoked for the camera upgrades on Apple’s new models.

But I’m most excited about two comparatively minor upgrades, too. The expanded Dynamic Island capabilities and a redesigned vapor chamber appeal to me as someone who is constantly on the move and needs glanceable information. Here’s why I think these upgrades might tempt me to upgrade to the 18 Pro Max.

More glanceable information in the Dynamic Island

The Dynamic Island is smaller on the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max (right) than last year’s 17 Pro Max (left).Patrick Holland/CNET

When I’m on the go, I’m almost always jumping between multiple apps. One minute it is Flightly to track my flights, another minute I’m checking routes on Google Maps and then waiting for my Uber ride to arrive. On my iPhone 17 Pro Max, the Dynamic Island tracks two Live Activities, but I need to swipe between the three apps to multitask. Apple is changing this with its new Pro iPhones.

With the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, the new Dynamic Island can expand to show up to three live activities simultaneously. It doesn’t stretch all the way to the screen edges. Instead, you get one main activity on the Dynamic Island with smaller circular icons on either side.

A preview of the three activities to be tracked by the Dynamic Island.Screenshot by CNET/Apple

This won’t change the way you use your iPhone, but I expect it to make multitasking easier with glanceable info right on top of your iPhone. The small icons likely won’t provide much information, but if I can get a navigation arrow alongside my Flighty updates and ETA for Uber rides, I’m sorted. The two icons also serve as shortcuts to open those apps, offering faster access than manually switching apps — which is common when I’m juggling my flight information while getting out of that rideshare vehicle.

A redesigned vapor chamber for better cooling

The iPhone 18 Pro has a larger vapor-cooling chamber.Screenshot by CNET/Apple

My iPhone 17 Pro Max gets warm to the touch when I’m navigating and using the camera app on my photo walks. It drains the battery faster than usual. That’s why I’m excited about the iPhone 18 Pro Max’s improved ability to keep itself cool during intensive periods like my constant photography.

The iPhone 18 Pro has a “next-generation” vapor chamber that’s three times the surface area of the one in the iPhone 17 Pro. Apple redesigned the phone’s interior so its A20 Pro processor can connect directly to the vapor chamber, which is claimed to continuously cycle deionized water throughout the system for “significant” improvements in cooling performance.

Theoretically, all of this could allow the A20 Pro chip to sustain higher performance for longer periods. I imagine it helping keep the phone cool on extended camera usage and navigation, and delivering longer battery life.

You can see the aperture physically open and close on the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max.Patrick Holland/CNET

Pro controls to take control of my photos

I’m not a professional photographer, but I love taking photos. I’m into street photography and portraits, and the iPhone 18 Pro’s new upgrades seem fantastic, at least on paper. While variable aperture would allow me to control the amount of light hitting the sensor, I’m more excited to try the Pro Controls.

So far, I’ve relied on third-party apps to take motion-blur photos, but I can finally do so within the iPhone 18 Pro’s Camera app itself. Apple is adding the ability to adjust the shutter speed from the viewfinder.

The new Pro controls will let you customize your camera and photo-taking experience by adding manual control options for changing the white balance, using a histogram to check exposure levels, changing the shutter speed and manually adjusting the aperture between four options (ƒ/1.48, ƒ/1.8, ƒ/2.8, and ƒ/4.0 f-stops). 

Pro controls on the iPhone 18 Pro can help capture more creative photos without needing any third-party apps.Screenshot by CNET/Apple

These Pro controls will allow me to take full control of how my image looks, rather than relying on Apple’s auto mode or processing to decide everything for me.

Sure, most Android phones have had this feature for years, which is why I carry an Ultra phone alongside my iPhone on9 every trip. However, the iPhone 18 Pro could finally make me ditch the second camera phone and carry just one device for my casual photography. 

These three upgrades have me stoked for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max. The redesigns that get me more glanceable information around the Dynamic Island, camera improvements that give me more control over my photography and improvements that will hopefully keep the phone from getting too warm will have an immediate impact on how I use the phone while running around the world.

title: Out of Pocket: Detailing our everyday carry
snippet: I love building a “kit,” a “pack,” a bag with enough stuff in it to make sure I am ready for every eventuality. I’m not talking about a survival kit per se, just some things that mean I am basically ready for any modern situation. more…
fullText:
I love building a “kit,” a “pack,” a bag with enough stuff in it to make sure I am ready for every eventuality. I’m not talking about a survival kit per se, just some things that mean I am basically ready for any modern situation.

EDC or Every Day Carry is basically part of my personality at this stage. It started with smartphones, moved on to earbuds, and steadily, like many of you, I accrued an assortment of gadgets, products, and things I found myself dragging with me everywhere.

I am constantly on the lookout for the next thing to enhance my EDC. I’m not alone in this; Andrew is in the same boat. We’re product people first and foremost, but practicality has to be a component before it becomes a bigger part of daily lives.

We figured that we’d share some of that intimate knowledge, driven by building packs for trade shows, travel, and just, well, hanging around.

	

So, this is Out of Pocket, our new series diving into what makes our EDC tick. Expect more deep dives into the kinds of things that are adjacent to your smartphone, the things that you carry every day, or brand new products that might pique your interest. After all, we all have our own specific EDC essentials. Here are a few of ours to hopefully get your own creative juices flowing…

My current kit (Damien)

The Sidebag – TomToc T33 (3.5L)

My search for the perfect sidebag has been, I’ll be honest, arduous. Day-to-day, I’m not much of a backpack guy, so a sling or a sidebag is the perfect accessory for all the little things I feel like I need. I already own a Bellroy Venture Ready sling, and while it’s awesome. It is just a little bit too small for a real EDC kit.

TomToc’s T33 sidebag is exponentially better with more pockets, exceptional internal organization, and interior sections. You could fit a small-ish water bottle or drink in the middle section, but netted segments mean I can throw in paracetamol or lip balm for easy access. There’s enough room for a really small tablet or notebook and documents in the back portion.

There’s a key carabiner so I can throw in my house keys and keychain right at the front. It’s stretchy enough to open a door and have the key snap back into the front pocket.

One of my must-haves on a sling is a body-facing “secret” pocket. When I’m traveling, my passport goes here so it’s accessible, but also harder for someone to try and slip their hand in – not that this has been a problem.

One of the most important things for me is that it’s waterproof. While it’s hot right now in England, we’re due a downpour. I like that all my stuff inside is safe and dry. The zippers are smooth, with waterproof seams, and there are lots of carabiner anchor points too, so you can attach a hat or a water bottle. It hits all the right notes, and I’ve abused it thoroughly, and it just wipes clean.

It’s super cheap for what it offers at under $45. My only gripe is that the color options aren’t all that extensive, but you could level that criticism at basically any sidebag. This is one that won’t break the bank.

Get the TomToc T33 sling

The Juice  – Anker Nano 5,000mAh power pack

Power banks are just so ubiquitous now that you can basically boil it down to what you want or need. Because I use the Pixel 11 Pro, I always want a Magsafe-compatible power bank around to slap to the back of the phone.

I had been using the Genki Energy Pack for almost a year now, and there were a number of reasons for that. Firstly, it looks awesome with the black and orange color scheme. Secondly, it’s Qi2 certified, so it does all the necessary handshake stuff required to get faster and more efficient charging speeds.

However, it’s blocky and bulky, so I switched it out recently for something a little lighter. I’m rocking the Anker Nano power bank now because it isn’t as bulky and has enough juice to give me a full charge on basically any phone I’m carrying.

There’s a tiny strip of LEDs that shows remaining battery level; it’s Qi2 certified, but that is limited to 15W. I use the solitary USB-C charging port if I need 20W and above, but most of the time it’s absolutely fine when you’re out and about. For what it’s worth, I carry a super short USB-C cable that’s like 10cm for that specific reason too.

I do think it’s a little pricey, but you can get it in different colours and mine has taken a beating over the year or slightly longer I’ve been using it. It’s just something that can slip on to the back of your phone without being huge or messing around with cables – which is something I appreciate.

Get the Anker Nano power bank

On-the-go entertainment – Boox Go 6 e-reader

I reviewed the Boox Go 6 e-reader almost two years ago, and since then, it has become a staple in my EDC setup. It’s just so small and inconspicuous that it basically lives in my sidebag.

As an e-reader, it’s nothing special. I’d even say it’s a little underpowered for what it offers, but the size and shape are what keep me coming back basically every single day. I basically leave it running the Kindle app or download some epub files, and it handles those absolutely fine. It is technically an Android tablet, so you can share files using Quick Share. I find this is great if you find something you want to read because you can just fire things over without messing with cables. Heck, I have hundreds of EPUBs that just work now, which is lovely. Even PDFs work just fine.

It’s under 300g with a magnetic flip case attached, so it’s not heavy by any stretch of the imagination. I have my eye on a few of the even smaller Magsafe e-readers, but at 6-inches this is like a pamphlet or an especially large coupon. Perfect for reading novels, documents, or even a downloaded webpage – not that I would recommend that!

A newer version has just been released that enables note-taking and various other improvements. I’m hoping to test drive that soon, but I have genuinely loved the compact design of the Go 6 and think I’d struggle to go back to a full-sized Kindle for that reason alone. It has come down in price to around $160, which isn’t cheap, but still not bad if you want something super small. That said, something even smaller might be better for just throwing into an even smaller sling bag…

Get the Boox Go 6 e-reader

Always available audio – USB-C earbuds

I simply hate not having some earbuds with me when I’m out of the house. I simply must be distracted with podcasts, YouTube Music, or if I want to take a call, I cannot live without a pair in my bag.

I usually have about 20 pairs of Bluetooth earbuds lying around my desk, but when the battery dies, they’re useless. I was so annoyed at a pair of buds dying mid-flight while traveling last year that I bought a random pair of USB-C earbuds from an airport vending machine to keep the music flowing. I think they’re from Xiaomi as there’s a little “Mi” logo embossed on the inline remote. I only paid like $16, but Belkin makes a pair that are $15 and reputable enough that I might pick up a pair as a spare.

Honestly, they sound fine. The threshold is that a pair of earbuds just needs to sound better than traffic or that dull airplane drone. These earbuds live in my bag as a last resort audio option, heck, they’re great to just share with someone if they’ve forgotten their own earbuds. They take up basically negligible space, too. When I’m done with them, I quickly wipe them with an alcohol pad, and they’re sterilized. Trust me, it’s worth having at least one backup option because the one time you need them, it’s a lifesaver. If you lose them, it’s not a big deal. Win-win in my book.

Get some cheap USB-C earbuds

Retro on the go – Gamesir Pocket Taco controller

If I’m taking a backpack, I usually try to make room for my Steam Deck or Switch 2, but if I’m going out for a few hours, I’ll usually stick to something much smaller. I love Gamesir’s range of controllers, but the Pocket Taco is one that, as a millennial gamer and Gameboy obsessive, I’m sticking with for now.

It clips onto your phone – don’t worry, it has rubber pads to stop scratches – and gives you real buttons to play games in portrait orientation like Nintendo intended back in the late 1980s. It really does feel like a DMG Game Boy in the best ways. Thankfully, there are more buttons that you can map so that you can play other emulators, not just Gameboy.

If you’re not a gamer, mobile or otherwise, this might not be for you, and that’s absolutely fine. For nerds of a certain “vintage,” you’ll probably love this as much as I do.

Get the Pocket Taco game controller

The extras – ‘stuff’ and ‘things’

We’re all humans, so we can’t just have cables and batteries in our bags. I carry a few other key things that are useful. Most of these are just cheap things that I’ve found are worth having.

After a trip to a city with questionable-quality streetlights, I picked up a little keychain torch that just attaches to my keys. Olight makes a ton of EDC lighting products, but I love the iMini 2 at just $20 because it can just go on my keys with the carabiner clip.

I just charge it every couple of months using the integrated USB-A plug at the back, and it lasts a lotng time despite the fact that it’s absolutely tiny. Detach to power on, then it magnetically snaps back into place, and the light turns off. Super useful if you don’t want to drain your smartphone’s battery, and it’s bright enough to light a small room. Sometimes I just use it to fine stuff I’ve dropped down the side of my car seats.

Get the Olight iMini 2 keychain flashlight

I have spilled tea and coffee on my clothes so many times that I started carrying around a Tide stain pen a while back, and it has saved many a shirt. It’s not going to get out huge stains, but it’s still nice to stop something from ruining your outfit. They’re around $15 for a 5-pack. I can’t recommend them highly enough because they’ve stopped so many of my shirts and t-shirts from getting completely ruined over the past few years.

On a similar note, I try to carry a microfiber cleaning cloth, alcohol cleaning pads, and napkins or tissues. Throw in some hand gel, lotion, a little sunscreen, and I’m covered for basically any eventuality.

My current kit (Andrew)

The backpack – Peak Design Travel Backpack 20L

Whether I step outside with a sling or my backpack is entirely down to whether I decide to tote my laptop along. I use a MacBook Air 13-inch, which has the smallest footprint one can reasonably expect a bag to fit. But even so, there is a true limit to the number of slings that can carry a small laptop. So if that’s coming with me, I’m taking the Peak Design Travel Backpack 20L.

The 20L variant has easily become my favorite backpack to lug around if I’m going with a heavier loadout. It weighs very little, and it’s completely unassuming. If there needs to be more on my back, it can expand slightly beyond that small capacity. But otherwise, I’m able to carry my laptop and a few essentials without worry.

The main compartment is great for just throwing random items in. When I’m using this bag, stuff doesn’t need to be organized as it would in a dedicated camera bag. I’m generally going to bring my tech pouch along, too. But that’s almost overkill because the top pocket has all of the same inner pockets for those little things I want to tag along.

It has all of the little creature comforts you’d want. Magnetic strap keepers, a pass-through for luggage handles, and an internal water bottle holder, so a giant container of liquid isn’t sloshing around way off balance. Overall, it’s simple but incredibly effective at what it does.

Get the Peak Design Travel 20L

The sidebag – Bellroy Lite Sling Mini

As for the sling, my rule states that I’ll swap to this if my laptop isn’t coming along. The Sling Lite Mini has the feel of an outdoor bag without so much of the look, so it flies under the radar more than a technical pack might. The outer material is strong and lightweight, but it doesn’t repel liquid as well as I’d hope it would. The internal pocket structure is simple, but efficient. The main pocket is plenty large enough for random items, and it’s complemented by a zipper pocket for thinner items. One of the gussets that let it expand is lined with a pocket I use to slip my Nomad titanium pen and handy USB ChargeKey. On the other side, I clip my knife and flashlight.

The best part about it being geared towards outdoor use is that it’s expandable. The gusseted construction keeps it compact, no matter how much you stuff in it. So even if it’s full, the shoulder strap pulls it tight so the overall profile is kept slim.

It’s tough and just easy to grab and go. I love this bag.

Neither is traditionally “cheap,” and Damien offers a great alternative with his TomToc sidebag. But at $79 for the sling and double that for the Travel Backpack, it’s a “buy it for life” sort of purchase.

Get the Bellroy Sling Lite Mini

The power – Baseus Qi2 25W

I generally don’t have the fear of running out of power with whatever phone I’m using. I wouldn’t say I’m an ultra-power user, but there are times when I just start to run out of steam on my Galaxy Fold 8 Ultra or Pixel 11. You can carry a slim charging brick, which I do anyway, or you can take a magnetic power bank.

I always carry the Baseus 10,000mAh Qi2.2 25W power bank with me. Because the Pixel has magnets on the back without the help of a case, I can always slap it on. If needed, I can plug the bank into something else via USB-C. Speeds aren’t really an issue, either, because it runs at 25W – right where the Pixel 10 Pro XL is rated, even if it doesn’t always charge that fast.

Baseus has slightly thinner options, but I prefer the charging speed I get with the 25W model. It just works when I need it, and it’s really not all that heavy.

Get the Baseus Qi2 power bank

The catalyst – Statik MagStak Pro USB-C cable

It’s kind of big, and it’s kind of bulky, but if I’m bringing a bag, I have little reason not to throw this in. Statik’s MagStack cable is a 100W magnetic cable that essentially coils itself back up every single time. It solves the issue of cables that are all over the place and are resistant to any coercion to get them back into shape.

I’ve been using the MagStack cable for the better part of a year, and it just refuses to lose it’s uniform appeal. I bring it with me whenever I can because it’s just easy to pack away, given you have the pocket space. Plus, I know it’s a high-speed cable, as opposed to all of my identical USB-C cables with varying levels of power delivery.

Get the Statik MagStack Pro cable

The wallet – Peak Design Mobile Slim

Yeah, maybe I am a Peak Design nerd. I can’t really help it. The design speaks to me on the photography side, as well as on the engineering side. I’ve been using the mobile slim wallet for what has to be three or four years. It’s almost time to replace it, because that once “Sun” yellow color has now darkened to a dijon.

It’s a standard slim pull-tab wallet. I hold a few cards in there, including a Google Find My Device tracker, unlike my European counterpart, who seems adamant that carrying a physical ID is no longer a normal part of society. Until Google Wallet can add my license without any potential governmental hiccups, I’m carrying a MagSafe wallet with me.

Get the Peak Design Mobile Wallet

The flat light – Olight ArkPro Ultra

I don’t know what it is about flashlights, but they come in clutch way more than you’d think. The ArcPro Ultra is technically a “flat” light, but it’s still sort of beefy. That doesn’t stop me from throwing it in my pocket or bags whenever I go out, even if it’s in the middle of the day and there’s no conceivable need to carry a torch.

Still, I’ve used it too many times to start leaving it behind. The battery essentially never dies, and I can beam up to 1,700 lumens with a simple double-tap. Plus, the slider to switch between UV, spotlight, and floodlight acts as a fantastic fidget toy.

Get the Olight ArcPro Ultra

title: Samsung reportedly considers early ‘Galaxy Z TriFold 2’ release in wake of iPhone Duo
snippet: In the wake of iPhone Duo, Samsung is reportedly considering an early release for a Galaxy Z TriFold sequel. more…
fullText:
In the wake of iPhone Duo, Samsung is reportedly considering an early release for a Galaxy Z TriFold sequel.

The Galaxy Z TriFold delivered a wild new form factor to Samsung’s lineup late last year, but it didn’t stick around for long. The TriFold made its US debut in January for $2,900 and was discontinued barely three months later.

There have been rumors flying around a “Galaxy Z TriFold 2” coming in 2027 alongside another new form factor, a slideable, but it sounds like that might be moved up following Apple’s iPhone Duo reveal. 

Leaker Lanzuk says that Samsung is “considering” an early “Galaxy Z TriFold 2” release, with the slideable also being moved up. An exact timeline is unclear, and it’s likely enough that the 2027 timeline will remain.

	

The post also claims that the TriFold sequel will be “thinner, lighter, and more durable” compared to the first generation, with a goal of having the price be “nearly identical.” While $2,899 is still no small price to pay, it’d be impressive if Samsung were able to keep pricing unchanged given the market forces at play, not to mention rumors that the first TriFold was sold at a loss. 

Would you buy a second-generation TriFold?

title: Googlebook pre-orders start on September 21
snippet: After previously teasing a fall timeframe, Google is set to open pre-orders for Googlebooks on Monday, September 21. more…
fullText:
After previously teasing a fall timeframe, Google is set to open pre-orders for Googlebooks on Monday, September 21.

The email blast to users who signed up for updates on the Android-based platform went out this morning. On September 21 at 9 a.m. ET, you’ll be able to pre-order the first Googlebook devices.

You can expect devices from Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo, with several leaking in recent weeks. By that date, Google will presumably detail the full operating system, including sharing what the actual name is. In May, we only got a preview.

Today’s teaser highlights the Magic Pointer that allows you to access Gemini immediately. This animation transforms into the light bar that all Googlebooks are expected to feature as their marquee branding element. Google has yet to share what exactly it will do. Compared to Chromebooks, this will be the primary brand on the cover. “Googlebooks” only appears on the left palm rest just below the keyboard. 

	

It’s not clear what the gap between pre-orders and device shipments will be, but launching before the holiday shopping season seems likely.

title: A NASA Scientist Found a Huge New Crater on the Moon by Accident
snippet: It’s unlikely another crater this big will be discovered in our lifetime.
fullText:
The moon has more than 2 million craters on its surface, but the overwhelming majority of the big ones happened long before humans ever started looking at it. That means when someone notices a new big crater, it’s a pretty big deal, and that’s exactly what happened when NASA’s Lunar Orbiter found a brand-new crater it had never seen before that was large enough to get someone’s attention.

The crater was spotted by NASA scientist Robert Wagner on a routine data-quality check and published in an article in Science Advances. Wagner says the object that crashed into the moon and created the crater likely hit sometime between April 11, 2024, and May 22, 2024, and was likely about the size of a six-story building. It left a rather sizable dent, which now has the distinction of being the biggest new crater ever spotted by NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. 

“I just stopped, dropped everything, and started looking into what that spot was,” Wagner said in a statement.

The LRO scans the entire moon’s surface once every 14 days, meaning humans have a constant stream of new data about the surface, and since the moon has no atmosphere, its pockmarked surface remains largely intact until another asteroid or meteor barrels into it. 

NASA says that the LRO has found approximately 1,000 new impact craters and over 100,000 other changes to the moon’s surface during its 17 years in service. Since the satellite can see craters only about 30 feet wide or larger, that also means many small impacts go virtually unnoticed, leaving the total number of changes to the moon’s surface a mystery.

One big hole

The new crater, circled in the left image, may not look like much, but it’s unlikely to happen again until the next century.NASA Goddard/Intuitive Machines/Robert Wagner

What makes this particular crater special is that it’s huge. At 728 feet wide, it’s more than twice the size of a football field, and at 141 feet deep is about the length of three yellow school buses stacked end to end. Impact craters that big don’t show up every day, every year or even every decade.

“Crater production models indicate that an impact of this magnitude is expected to occur only once every 132 years on the moon,” Wagner wrote in the article. “As such, this event constitutes a statistically rare, effectively one-in-a-lifetime observation.” 

It’s the latest in a pretty busy year for the moon, which had human visitors for the first time in 50 years with the Artemis II mission before an abandoned SpaceX rocket crash-landed into it, which left a crater substantially smaller than the one Wagner found.

NASA named the crater McGetchin, after Tom McGetchin, a scientist who became the director of the Lunar Science Institute in 1977, shortly before his death in 1979.

title: Judge scrutinizes Musk’s move to drop Apple from antitrust lawsuit involving OpenAI
snippet: Federal judge Mark Pittman wants details on any agreement that may have led Elon Musk’s companies to drop their antitrust claims against Apple. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Federal judge Mark Pittman wants details on any agreement that may have led Elon Musk’s companies to drop their antitrust claims against Apple. Here are the details.

Judge wants to see any Apple agreement

Earlier this week, X and SpaceXAI submitted a motion to voluntarily dismiss with prejudice their claims against Apple in the case they brought against Apple and OpenAI last year.

According to the original filing, Apple and OpenAI were colluding to keep competing AI apps from gaining visibility on the App Store, as a result of their agreement to integrate ChatGPT into Siri and Apple Intelligence. Apple and OpenAI rejected the claims.

In its filing earlier this week, X and SpaceXAI said only that they had “resolved their claims in this Action against” Apple, stressing that they did not seek to dismiss their claims against OpenAI.

Now, as first reported by POLITICO, Judge Mark Pittman, who has been overseeing the case, has ordered X and SpaceXAI to provide the court with “any agreement or combination of agreements with Apple that relate to the resolution of Plaintiffs’ claims against Apple in this litigation.”

The order came in response to an emergency motion filed by OpenAI seeking to compel X and SpaceXAI to produce their agreement resolving the dispute with Apple. Pittman also ordered the companies to respond to OpenAI’s motion by noon on September 17.

title: Amazon-owned Zoox’s 100-robotaxi limit in Nevada is about to disappear
snippet: An updated permit shows the 100-cap will expire later this month just as competition in Las Vegas heats up.
fullText:
A regulatory cap limiting Zoox to 100 robotaxis in Nevada is set to expire this month, clearing the way for the Amazon-owned company to expand its commercial fleet of custom-built robotaxis in Las Vegas just as competition heats up. 

The Nevada Transportation Authority (NTA) permit that imposed the 100-vehicle cap is set to expire September 25, TechCrunch has learned. An NTA official and a Zoox spokesperson confirmed the change, which is also outlined in an updated permit.

This doesn’t mean Las Vegas is about to be inundated with hundreds of Zoox robotaxis. But it does give Zoox more freedom to grow — and at a critical moment. Waymo recently launched a commercial service in Las Vegas, while Tesla and Uber have secured their own driverless ride-hailing permits. 

Today, Zoox has about 100 custom-built robotaxis — cube-like vehicles that lack steering wheels and pedals — spread across four U.S. cities, including Austin and Miami. The bulk of the fleet is in Las Vegas and San Francisco. And for now, Las Vegas remains the only city where Zoox is charging for rides. Zoox must still obtain another permit from California regulators before it can charge for passengers there. 

Zoox began charging for robotaxi rides in Las Vegas last month after receiving a temporary exemption from certain federal motor vehicle safety standards from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).

That exemption was crucial for Zoox because unlike Waymo, its robotaxis were designed without a steering wheel, pedals, or other traditional and federally mandated controls. The commercial exemption allows Zoox to deploy up to 2,500 vehicles per year for the next two years.

It’s unclear how quickly Zoox will take advantage of its newfound freedom in Nevada. A Zoox spokesperson declined to say how many robotaxis the company plans to add to its Las Vegas fleet or even how many are in operation there today. Robotaxi Tracker, which collects data on autonomous vehicles, estimates Zoox has more than 30 vehicles operating in the city. 

The spokesperson told TechCrunch that Zoox plans to steadily increase the size of its robotaxi fleet over the next several months “to meet the high demand in Las Vegas and other markets.” 

Zoox will have lots of company, no matter how fast it expands. In August, the NTA approved three permits that will allow Tesla, Uber, and Waymo to operate commercial robotaxi services in Clark County, home to Las Vegas. Together, the permits could bring up to 7,000 robotaxis to the area over the next 12 months.

Waymo has wasted little time acting on that permit. The company opened its robotaxi service to customers in Las Vegas earlier this month. Waymo told TechCrunch at the time that it would start with “dozens” of its new Ojai minivan robotaxis in a 23-square-mile area that includes the Strip south of Highway 589 and into Boulder Junction.

title: GM just found the ‘sweet spot’ for supporting Android Auto & CarPlay [Gallery]
snippet: GM has been stubbornly standing by its decision to axe Android Auto and Apple CarPlay from many of its newer vehicles in recent years, despite loud and constant negative feedback from consumers. In its latest software update for two new trucks, GM has found the “sweet spot” for implementing Android Auto and CarPlay, but it’s unclear if that compromise will extend to other vehicles. more…
fullText:
GM has been stubbornly standing by its decision to axe Android Auto and Apple CarPlay from many of its newer vehicles in recent years, despite loud and constant negative feedback from consumers. In its latest software update for two new trucks, GM has found the “sweet spot” for implementing Android Auto and CarPlay, but it’s unclear if that compromise will extend to other vehicles. 

A new software experience – based on Android Automotive / Google built-in – debuting in the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado and 2027 GMC Sierra will see GM’s software not only get a nice new coat of paint, but also some welcome functionality. As detailed by CNBC, the update will “proactively surface relevant controls” such as call controls and even a garage door opener. Both vehicles have plenty of physical controls, too.

The biggest news here, though, is GM finding a new way to implement Android Auto and CarPlay integration.

GM announced in 2023 that it would remove phone projection systems from its vehicles while embracing Android Automotive and native functionality in its infotainment system, a decision that has not been positively embraced by customers. While GM has not backed down from this change on its electric vehicles, many of its vehicles still support both platforms. 

	

The change here is that the Silverado and Sierra will support Android Auto and CarPlay, but in a new windowed mode. The projection appears on a part of the display, with aspects of the native infotainment coming through around the sides so you can still easily control parts of the car that projection systems cannot without actually closing anything. 

Speaking to The Verge, GM group product manager for Google built-in, projection, and profiles Colin McCormick explained that this is the “sweet spot.”

I think we’re landing in a spot where… we don’t have a customer that has to decide, “Oh, I’m going to use projection, or, oh, I want to use the native system…” That’s our sweet spot.

That said, there’s no word here on whether or not GM will actually bring Android Auto and CarPlay back to more of its vehicles. Gas-powered vehicles remain with support for phone projection, but that’s still missing in its EVs, including the latest Chevy Bolt that launched earlier this year.

In its latest software update for two new trucks, GM has found the “sweet spot” for implementing Android Auto and CarPlay, but it’s unclear if that compromise will extend to other vehicles.

A new software experience – based on Android Automotive / Google built-in – debuting in the 2027 Chevrolet Silverado and 2027 GMC Sierra will see GM’s software not only get a nice new coat of paint, but also some welcome functionality. As detailed by CNBC, the update will “proactively surface relevant controls” such as call controls and even a garage door opener. Both vehicles have plenty of physical controls, too.

title: Apple will let EU apps use less-alarming tracking-consent screens
snippet: Apple is changing its App Tracking Transparency prompts in parts of Europe after competition regulators said the system favored Apple over third-party apps, giving developers more flexibility over how they ask users for tracking consent.
fullText:
As a result of a multi-year antitrust probe by Germany’s federal competition regulator and others, Apple has agreed to modify the requirements for apps on its platforms that ask for consent to track the user across other apps or websites.

Regulators said this system, known as App Tracking Transparency, or ATT, had favored Apple over third-party apps, since Apple allows its own apps to use consumers’ data from its ecosystem without requiring a consent screen.

The new agreements with select European competition authorities don’t do away with the need to prompt users, or when that prompt is to be shown. Instead, they allow app developers whose software is distributed in the EU to display an alternative consent screen that includes modified formatting, language, and the option to link out to “additional information” about why the app is requesting this permission, among other things.

Apple’s compliance involves over half-a-dozen changes that attempt to make these ATT consent screens less scary to end users. This includes showing them as full-page screens, not pop-ups; removing the word “track”; changing the choice buttons to “Allow” and “Reject” instead of “Allow” and “Ask App Not to Track”; changing the colors and formatting; and more. Plus, developers can offer users more detailed information through a clickable link, explaining how they use this data and why it’s being requested.

The iPhone maker says that, due to legal requirements, only the alternative version of the system prompt will be available to apps distributed in Germany, France, Italy, Poland, and Romania.

Users typically respond to consent screens by asking apps not to track them, which hurts ad-supported businesses, like Meta, while boosting Apple’s own. In short, the apps asking for such permissions do so because it lets them show personalized advertising, which generates more revenue, helping the app developer to make money.

Apple, however, argued that these consent screens help protect consumer privacy, even though it permits its own apps to display personalized ads based on the data they collect from its ecosystem.

The company said it will now allow app developers distributing to the EU to re-prompt their EU users one year after the user’s previous choice in their ATT consent screen.

title: WhatsApp starts rolling out new in-chat search button on iOS
snippet: Following a few weeks of beta testing, WhatsApp is now rolling out its new in-chat search button to iPhone users. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Following a few weeks of beta testing, WhatsApp is now rolling out its new in-chat search button to iPhone users. Here are the details.

Early last month, WhatsApp started testing a new search button in the bottom-right corner of the in-chat interface, making it easier to start a search.

Up until now, in-chat search required users to tap on the contact or group name at the top of the conversation, select the search option from the chat info screen, and then enter their query after being taken back to the main chat.

An in-chat search button, by contrast, streamlines the process by letting users start searching without leaving the conversation.

Now, WABetaInfo reports that WhatsApp is officially rolling out the in-chat search button, though it appears in a different location than it did during beta testing.

Inage: WABetaInfo

Here’s WABetaInfo:

The new search button appears at the top of the screen when users scroll up through the conversation. When users return to the bottom of the chat, the button disappears again. It shows up contextually, only when it is useful. Users who see the button can tap it to activate search mode directly within the conversation. As soon as users enable search mode, they can type a keyword and find matching messages without leaving the chat. The search mode works just like the existing one, so users who are already familiar with it will not have to learn anything new.

WABetaInfo notes that the new shortcut is available across individual chats, group chats, and channels. In all three cases, the button appears near the top of the screen when users scroll up through the conversation or channel, and disappears again when they return to the bottom.

As with most WhatsApp feature rollouts, the new search button may take some time to reach everyone.

fullText:
If you’re anything like me, you’ve been all-in on smart lights for years. I almost never use light switches anymore and the luxury I’ve grown used to is immediately made apparent when I spend a night away from home. That said, smart lighting has continued to evolve far beyond the basic bulbs I’ve grown used to, and this was plain as day when I got my hands on the new Linkind Smart Light Stick.

First and foremost, these bulbs pack Matter compatibility for simple controls, but the perks really come to life when you tap into the AiDot app. This is where you can take advantage of addressable zones within the bulb, which sort of blew my mind. I also love the clean cylindrical look of these bulbs, which I will showcase down below.

The first thing that stood out to me when unboxing it was the hardware design. Rather than sticking to the familiar pear shape of standard household bulbs, Linkind opted for a clean, frosted cylinder. For this reason, I really think it will look great in frosted and transparent fixtures alike.

Matter-compatible bulbs with rich app customization

The setup process was refreshingly straightforward. As shown in the screenshots, grabbing the AiDot app and running through the pairing sequence took about a minute or so, and I was relieved straight away when I saw that the app actually had solid ratings. While Matter certification allows users to skip third-party apps entirely, skipping AiDot would cause you to miss out on a lot of the features that an app like AiDot can offer.

	

As you can see below, the number of available scenes is sort of obscene. It was a little overwhelming to see the number of options, but it’s easy to create favorites, which I’ll certainly be doing so it is easy to switch for whatever holiday season we are in the middle of.

To put these bulbs through their paces, I installed them across three different fixtures. First up was the pergola and hot tub area. Transparent wall mounted lanterns along the white lattice frame gave the Light Sticks plenty of room to show off. I then added them to one of the lamp posts in my yard, followed by the lamp that resides in my home office.

Hero feature is the customizable flame effect

Easily the coolest trick up the Light Stick’s sleeve is its built-in flame simulation. Rather than settling for a basic pixelated flicker, the frosted cylindrical design diffuses light to deliver a much more authentic look than I tend to see with other bulbs, especially when dropped into an open fixture like my office lamp or outdoor lanterns.

Setup is straight forward, allowing me to quickly customize the look I was after. I did my best to capture it in action in the video below. In my opinion, the video doesn’t quite do it justice, as I think it looks much better in person.

Seasonal curb appeal with festive scenes

Until now, I’ve been going with warm white lighting 100% of the time. With Linkind Smart Light Stick Pro, I don’t have a reason to forego shaking up the look of my space when the seasons change or a holiday arrives.

While there are plenty of pre-made dynamic scenes to pick from, the DIY tab in the AiDot app is where the hardware really shines. As mentioned earlier, there are individually addressable zones, offering up 50 individual areas you can customize. I was able to use the app to create a neat color effect in under a minute, and you can see the UI below.

The settings above lead to another neat animation that I tried to capture on video. Like before, while it looks great on video, it’s even better in person. I took the lamp shade off and you can see that the bulb looks great even when fully on display, which is something I cannot say for a lot of the other smart bulbs out there.

And if you want clearer examples of what the bulbs actually look like in person, check out the official footage in the video below. It highlights a wider variety of dynamic presets, from festive holiday scenes to subtle ambient glows. It really drives home just how versatile these are compared to standard, single-color smart bulbs.

Pricing and availability

If you want to step up your outdoor or indoor lighting like I have, head over to Linkind’s website to find these bulbs (and all of the others they sell). You can pick up the bulbs directly on Amazon, where they are currently selling for $39.99.

title: Flash floods can strike without warning — this new technology could change that
snippet: On the morning of June 9th, Laura Lin was working from her home in Lanesville, a rural southern Indiana town about 15 miles from the Kentucky border.
